frontier_links: 7.2 Automated memory management. Token-level managers already treat delete and update as basic operations: Mem0 uses ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP, Memory-R1 learns those operations with RL, and Zep invalidates superseded edges. Protected-set parametric editors offer only ADD. The ledger supplies the missing UPDATE/DELETE primitive for weights, and any learned policy over parametric memory would need it.

Trustworthy memory [ABS, SEC]. A ghost value is a stale-memory hallucination. A wrong or poisoned edit gets protected by the same mechanism and then resists correction. The ledger also serves as an audit trail of which writes the weights currently defend.

Third-party critique [SEC, lower reliability]: the survey glosses over keeping a parametric memory in sync with a token-level DB as both change. The ledger is exactly that sync layer: a token-level shadow of the weight store, updated on every write and every supersession.

Section 4 dynamics: F, E and R 'need not be invoked at every time step'. Compaction at a garbage ratio tau is a periodic consolidation schedule, and the downdate-vs-compaction cost frontier is a concrete instance of it.
mapped.survey_claim_tested: The survey files model editing under Evolution/Updating for parametric memory [SNIP]. The card can falsify this for the current state-of-the-art family. Its prediction is that history-aware protected-set editors (AlphaEdit's soft Gram; BetaEdit/OrthoEdit/EvoEdit hard projectors) are append-only Formation operators, not Updating operators. A revision realizes only about 1/(n+1) of its update (soft) or almost none (hard), and the old value persists, so real updating needs an explicit forgetting step (the downdate). A secondary target is the trade-off reported by [SEC] (less reliable), that parametric memory 'suffers catastrophic forgetting'. For revised facts in null-space editors the card predicts the opposite failure, over-retention, with degradation that scales with superseded writes rather than total writes.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: AlphaEdit: Null-Space Constrained Knowledge Editing for Language Models
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Base method, and the soft-Gram target of the diagnosis: its official cache_c is an additive sum with no per-fact identity. It is already the card's main baseline. The survey lists it as the most recent editor in the cell.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Neighboring Perturbations of Knowledge Editing on Large Language Models
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Not in the card yet, and the most useful listed addition. ICML 2024; the PEAK benchmark plus the APP add-on; run on GPT-2 XL among others (verified by search). It studies the mirror case. When a new answer is appended to a one-to-many fact, editors erode answers that should stay live. The card's case is supersession, where the old answer should die but stays protected. Together the two make a 2x2 (old value live/dead x protection kept/removed). PEAK is the natural control showing the ledger must not garbage-collect on appends.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: WISE: Rethinking the Knowledge Memory for Lifelong Model Editing of Large Language Models
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Already a baseline, but the plan describes it wrongly as a 'codebook [that] replaces the value on key collision'. Per search, WISE edits a side memory: each batch of edits goes into random-mask parameter subspaces, which are then merged, with a router choosing main or side memory. Whether a re-edit overwrites the old shard or coexists with it is undocumented. Treat WISE as a measured comparator, not an assumed-immune one.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: ELDER: Enhancing Lifelong Model Editing with Mixture-of-LoRA
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: A lifelong editor without a Gram matrix. Its routing loss sends inputs carrying the same knowledge to the same LoRA allocation, so re-edits may refresh that allocation rather than accumulate garbage (an inference; unverified). It reports GPT-2 XL results. It is a cheap non-protected-set comparator if its code runs.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Zep: A Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: The token-level analogue of the card's fix. On contradiction, Graphiti/Zep invalidates the old edge without deleting it, using bi-temporal valid/transaction timestamps, so point-in-time queries still work (verified by search, secondary sources). This is the model for keeping history in the ledger while removing it from the weights' protected set.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Mem0: Building production-ready ai agents with scalable long-term memory
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Token-level ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP memory operations. These frame the card's claim that parametric editors expose only ADD. Cite for positioning; not a baseline.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Memory-R1: Enhancing Large Language Model Agents to Manage and Utilize Memories via Reinforcement Learning
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Learns the same CRUD operations with RL over a token-level store, which shows the field treats DELETE/UPDATE as first-class operations. A learned manager over parametric memory would need the card's primitive first. Positioning only.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Towards Lifelong Dialogue Agents via Timeline-based Memory Management
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: From recall of the paper, not re-checked: it argues against deleting outdated memories and links them into timelines instead. This is a counter-position to 'garbage collection'. Address it by GC'ing only the protection in the weights while keeping history as token-level timeline records (refinement 5).

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Fast Model Editing at Scale
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: MEND: a hypernetwork editor with no protected set. It shows the pathology is specific to protected-set editors. Optional reference only; MEND's known sequential-editing collapse makes it a poor baseline.

mapped.reframed_title: Parametric Memory Without Delete: Superseded Writes Block Fact Revision in Null-Space Editors, and a Ledger That Lets Them Forget
mapped.reframed_one_liner: History-aware null-space editors are append-only parametric memories. Every past write stays protected, and two writes to the same (subject, relation) share a key under any prompt-conditioned key design. So a revision, or the correction of a wrong edit, realizes only about 1/(n+1) of its update under a soft Gram penalty, is almost fully blocked under a hard projector, and leaves the old value as a protected ghost. A token-level write ledger fixes this. It invalidates superseded writes Zep-style: their protection is downdated out of the weights, while their history is kept as text. It must not fire on appends (the PEAK case). With it, degradation should track live facts rather than total writes.
changes: Headline the claim in survey terms: 'protected-set editors implement Formation, not Updating'. The main figure becomes a 2x2: old value {still live: PEAK append | dead: supersession} x protection {kept | downdated}. Prediction: downdating helps supersession and hurts appends. Turn the plan's same-subject negative control into the PEAK half of this figure. PEAK-CF was run on GPT-2 XL, so it plugs into the existing GPT2-XL setup for about 10 GPU-hours.

Make the GC rule cardinality-aware. Downdate on supersession of a functional (s,r). Keep protection when a one-to-many relation gets an extra object. Add a kill/pivot clause: if downdating on PEAK appends does NOT hurt, protection of edited same-subject keys is doing no useful work, and the paper pivots to 'edited-key protection is unnecessary' (still a publishable negative result).

Add 'correcting a wrong edit' as the headline use case alongside career/marriage chains. It needs no new data: AToKe-ME's 73 A->B->A reversion chains, plus CounterFact pairs edited to the counterfactual and then back to the true object. This is the n=1 case. The prediction is about 50% realized per layer (soft) or near-zero (hard). It ties the paper to the survey's trustworthy-memory frontier (poisoned or mistaken edits that resist correction).

Separate address collision from garbage. Add one ablation with the ROME/MEMIT 'last-token' key setting instead of 'subject_last'; it is a config change, first in the CPU toy, then one GPU run of about 3 GPU-hours. Relation-aware keys should fix the different-relation interference that S2RKE and RoSE study, but not same-(s,r) supersession, because the prompt is identical. This pre-empts the reviewer response 'just fix the key design'.

Keep history in text, not weights (Zep-style invalidation). The ledger stores superseded (s, r, o, valid interval) records. Time-qualified queries are answered by inserting the matching ledger record into the prompt, and current queries by the weights. Evaluate on AToKe time-qualified prompts against PRISM Edit's parametric approach. This turns risk 7 ('GC discards history') into a cross-form result for about 2-3 GPU-hours of inference, and answers the THEANINE-style objection to deletion.

Reorder the GPU pilot. Run BetaEdit vanilla vs +stale-key removal on GPT2-XL first, then AlphaEdit soft-Gram. Near-total blocking under a hard projector is the larger, more margin-robust effect, and it targets the current state of the art. The z-margin absorption risk lives mainly in the soft-Gram case, so the GO decision should not rest on it alone.

Answer the survey critique that simple baselines are undervalued with an honest brute-force baseline. Cache each fact's z target in the ledger so compaction (re-solving all live facts from W0) costs only forward passes plus a linear solve. Report the accuracy-vs-compute frontier of downdate, periodic compaction (tau in {0.1, 0.25, 0.5}) and per-write full re-solve. If frequent compaction is nearly free and as good, the paper's contribution narrows to the diagnosis plus the scaling law; state that up front.

Add a one-row token-level reference: the ledger's current value placed in context (in-context editing) on the same chains. It bounds what a token-level store with UPDATE achieves. It also forces the paper to say why parametric revision matters: closed-book, on-device, or store-to-weights consolidation as in cards #3 and #9.

Fix the plan's baseline descriptions. WISE is a sharded side memory whose subspaces are merged, not a codebook that replaces values on collision. GRACE's behavior on conflicting labels at (near-)identical keys should be measured, not assumed. Measure both on revision chains rather than citing them as immune.

Stay within the <=1.5B constraint: drop the Llama3-8B confirmation and use GPT2-XL plus phi-1.5 only. Qwen2.5-1.5B is optional, if BetaEdit's code supports it. The PEAK runs, the key-design ablation and the ledger-history evaluation add about 15 GPU-hours. Dropping Llama3-8B and the 80GB card offsets the 20-30 GPU-hours the second-round re-check added for BetaEdit/OrthoEdit/EvoEdit. The total stays at about 150 GPU-hours on one 24-48GB card.

In related work, write for the agent-memory audience. Token-level factual memory has CRUD (Mem0, Memory-R1) and temporal invalidation (Zep). The survey's parametric factual cell (AlphaEdit, WISE, ELDER) has no delete. The ledger is the token-to-parametric sync layer the survey leaves open. Do not claim a new memory architecture; claim a missing operator and a diagnosis of what its absence costs.

mapped.rationale: The survey does not weaken #1, but it does not validate novelty either. The cell is sparse only because the agent-memory list stops at AlphaEdit (2024/10) and omits every 2025-26 history-aware null-space editor the card targets. The novelty case therefore rests on the earlier searches, and the existing must-reads (BetaEdit's analysis section and 2606.26783) still gate the project. The survey adds four useful things at almost no compute cost. (1) A falsifiable framing: model editing is filed under Updating, while the card predicts that protected-set editors are append-only. (2) A listed paper, 'Neighboring Perturbations of Knowledge Editing on Large Language Models' (PEAK), that turns the plan's weak negative control into a 2x2 main result and makes the GC rule cardinality-aware. (3) A token-level template for the fix and for the history problem (Zep invalidation; Mem0/Memory-R1 CRUD), which turns 'GC discards history' into a cross-form strength. (4) A trustworthy-memory use case, correcting wrong or poisoned edits, that raises impact above 'revision chains on GPT2-XL'. The main risks are unchanged and should be stated plainly. AlphaEdit's z-margin may absorb the soft-Gram attenuation. BetaEdit may already handle reappearing keys. The fix is a rank-1 downdate, and cheap periodic compaction may match it, in which case the paper rests on the diagnosis and the live-facts scaling law. The survey's framing also makes 'why not keep revisable facts in a token-level store?' an obvious reviewer question. The added in-context reference row and a clear statement of when parametric revision is needed (closed-book, on-device, store-to-weights consolidation) must answer it. Net: still the fastest Tier-A paper, now better positioned and within the <=1.5B constraint. Searches used (2 of 3 were on survey-listed overlaps): PEAK https://arxiv.org/pdf/2401.17623 and https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/ma24h.html; WISE https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/60960ad78868fce5c165295fbd895060-Abstract.html; ELDER https://arxiv.org/pdf/2408.11869; Zep/Graphiti invalidation https://mintlify.com/getzep/graphiti/concepts/temporal-model and https://blog.getzep.com/beyond-static-knowledge-graphs/.

frontier_links: Multimodal memory for embodied agents [ABS]: a persistent latent scene memory from RGB streams, reused across sessions
Memory for world models [SEC]: the CUT3R state is a latent scene model, and banking plus warm start makes that world model persist across sessions
7.1 retrieval -> generation [TOC]: probing a banked state with CUT3R's virtual-view raymap generates the expected geometry at a query pose instead of retrieving stored images

mapped.survey_claim_tested: The survey claims that short-term vs long-term memory 'emerge from the temporal patterns with which formation, evolution and retrieval are engaged', not from separate architectural modules [SNIP]. Card #2 tests this directly: the identical latent object, with no architectural change, becomes long-term memory only by changing when it is written (snapshot) and retrieved (warm start/restore). Confirm: a banked state warm-starts session 2 and beats byte-matched stored frames. Falsify, or at least qualify: the state is useful only after explicit Sim(3) re-anchoring, or loses to images as viewpoint distance grows. That would show spatial latent memory is frame-bound, a property the survey's form taxonomy does not model. Secondary: it tests the critique recorded in the third-party note that 'latent memory is just state or caching, not true memory' [SEC], through the state vs source-frames control.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: M+: Extending MemoryLLM with Scalable Long-Term Memory
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: The closest listed analog of the snapshot bank. Hidden-state memory pushed out of the short-term pool is moved to a CPU long-term store instead of being discarded, and a co-trained retriever brings relevant latents back to the GPU (checked by search). Differences: it is trained (LoRA read/write adapters plus retriever), the retrieved latents are attended to rather than substituted for the live state, it works within a single text stream, and it has no coordinate frame.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Memorizing Transformers
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Stores past KV latents in an external memory and reads them by kNN attention. This is the canonical 'attend to retrieved latents' integration, which the card does not currently test against its substitute/blend operators.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Augmenting Language Models with Long-Term Memory
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: LongMem: cached past KV in a memory bank with a trained side network for retrieval and fusion. Same latent-repository pattern; it is trained and contains no recurrent-state substitution.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Memory${}^3$: Language Modeling with Explicit Memory
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Argues that externalized sparse KV memory is a cheaper format than re-reading source text (RAG). That is the LLM analog of card #2's core question: is a stored latent state better per byte and per compute than re-feeding its source frames?

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Context as Memory: Scene-Consistent Interactive Long Video Generation with Memory Retrieval
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Keeps past frames as raw memory and retrieves them by camera field-of-view overlap with the current pose (checked by search). This is exactly the 'store images, re-feed them' pole that card #2's controls stand for, so its FOV-overlap selection should become the image-store baseline.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: MemoryVLA: Perceptual-Cognitive Memory in Vision-Language-Action Models for Robotic Manipulation
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: A latent memory bank for an embodied model, with retrieval, gated fusion and consolidation. When the bank overflows, it merges the most similar adjacent entries by averaging (checked by search). This is a listed bank-management baseline and an analog of the R3 blend. It is trained and works within one episode.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: XMem: Long-Term Video Object Segmentation with an Atkinson-Shiffrin Memory Model
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Working-to-long-term consolidation of latent feature memory within a video. It is the listed precedent for promoting latent working memory, but it has no cross-session reuse and no recurrent-state restore.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Towards General Continuous Memory for Vision-Language Models
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: A factual-latent memory formed from visual input (continuous memory embeddings for a VLM). Same cell as the card's target, but it uses a trained compressor and no geometry.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Mem2Ego: Empowering Vision-Language Models with Global-to-Ego Memory for Long-Horizon Embodied Navigation

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Embodied VideoAgent: Persistent Memory from Egocentric Videos and Embodied Sensors Enables Dynamic Scene Understanding
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Persistent scene memory updated when the scene changes. This is an explicit-form analog of the change-gated release (Evolution: Updating) planned for RIO10.

mapped.reframed_title: More than a cache? Promoting a frozen CUT3R/TTT3R state from working memory to cross-session scene memory

Then test, at matched bytes and forward passes, whether the stored latent state beats re-feeding FOV-selected stored frames. On one side, the snapshot: roughly 1.2 MB if the state is 768 tokens x 768 dims in fp16, to be confirmed in code, with 0 extra passes. On the other, k JPEG keyframes of equal total bytes (about 15-25 at 512 px) re-fed through a cold state, at k passes. mapped.rationale: Read critically, the survey cuts both ways for card #2. First, it shows the card overstates part of its mechanism. Copying latent state to a CPU bank, retrieving it by key and evicting under a budget is an established latent-repository pattern in the survey's list. M+ moves overflowed hidden states to CPU and retrieves them with a co-trained retriever; Memorizing Transformers and LongMem retrieve cached KV; MemoryVLA keeps an embodied latent bank with merge-based consolidation. So the 'Idea' bullets and the coverage-eviction sweep read as a domain transfer. The eviction part is also unmotivated, since a snapshot is about 1 MB. Second, the question the card can answer is absent from the survey and maps onto two of its open points. One is the claim that short- vs long-term memory come from the timing of F/E/R rather than from architecture. The other is the critique that latent memory is 'just state/caching'. Both are tested by the card's state-vs-source-frames control. That control is currently too weak to carry the claim: one keyframe or the last 8 keyframes, at unequal bytes and compute. Rebuilding it as a byte- and pass-matched frontier with Context-as-Memory-style FOV selection makes the result decisive either way. Adding R4 (attend to retrieved latents) and the raymap probe ties it to the survey's integration vocabulary and its retrieval-to-generation frontier at under 5 extra GPU-h. Narrowing the GO to cross-session and cutting the eviction sweep makes the project cheaper (~100 GPU-h, pilot ~10-12 GPU-h) and keeps it away from the crowded within-session space (Scal3R, ReCal3R, Info3R). The survey's lack of 3D papers is not evidence of novelty in 3D; the competitive threats are unchanged from the card's own prior-work list. Caveats: the 'temporal patterns' quote and the third-party critique come from snippets and a secondary note, not the PDF. The descriptions of M+, MemoryVLA and Context as Memory were checked by search snippets only. CUT3R's raymap probing, and the state size (if it is 768x768 dims), should be confirmed in code before the pilot.

mapped.cell_density: The source cell, factual x token-level, is dense (84 listed). The target cell, factual x parametric, is moderate (16), mostly editors and plug-in memories: AlphaEdit, WISE, ELDER, MEND, Memory Decoder, MLP Memory. The soft-address arm touches factual x latent, which is sparse (8). No listed paper does store-to-weights consolidation followed by pruning the store; the nearest are SELF-PARAM, MAC and Memory Decoder. That gap is partly an artifact of the list's Jan 2026 cutoff: Dual-Layer Agentic Memory (Aug 2026) and EVAF (Jun 2026) already sit there. The sparse cell therefore overstates novelty.
frontier_links: 7.1 From memory retrieval to memory generation: an address-only entry replaces retrieving the content with cued regeneration from the weights. The eviction gate measures, fact by fact, when that switch is safe (eviction regret).

7.2 Automated memory management: the delayed, address-cued self-test is a cheap, checkable DELETE criterion. It can be compared with age/LRU heuristics and with Mem0/Memory-R1-style ADD/UPDATE/DELETE operations, which delete on redundancy or contradiction and never check whether the weights already hold the fact.

7.8 Human-cognitive connections: the no-cue gate (Dual-Layer) corresponds to standard systems consolidation, where the index becomes dispensable. The address state corresponds to hippocampal indexing or multiple-trace retention. HippoRAG borrows indexing theory, but its index points to passages; here the index points into the weights.
Trustworthy memory: evicting text loses provenance (no supporting text to show), redirection errors are confident hallucinations, and deleting the text does not delete the fact from the weights.
Third-party critique of the survey (it glosses over keeping parametric and token-level memory in sync as both change): this card is literally a synchronization operator between the two forms.
mapped.survey_claim_tested: Mainly 7.1 (retrieval -> generation). The card is a falsifiable, per-fact test of whether a factual store can stop retrieving content and instead regenerate it from the weights on a short cue. The claim fails for consolidated facts if, at >=5x context-token reduction, eviction regret exceeds 20%, or if shuffled-code, format-prime or optimized-suffix controls recover as much as the address. A secondary claim comes only from [SEC] summaries, so it is less reliable: the survey's trade-off that parametric memory is efficient but suffers catastrophic forgetting. The card separates storage loss from access loss. Cue recovery R>=0.5 with controls <=0.15 on facts that were learned and later lost would show that sequential-SFT forgetting is largely an access failure, an argument for hybrid token+parametric forms over choosing one form.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Self-Updatable Large Language Models by Integrating Context into Model Parameters
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: SELF-PARAM (ICLR 2025, checked via search this session) trains the no-context model to match the with-context model's predictions on generated QA, using KL. It needs no extra parameters and no external memory, and it reports retention under sequential injection. It is a better write operator for the same store-to-weights move. If its writes keep facts reachable without a cue, the address state is unnecessary, so it must be a baseline write method.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Pretraining with hierarchical memories: separating long-tail and common knowledge
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Checked via search. Long-tail facts are stored in memory blocks fetched by context (an 18M block from a 4.6B bank); context-selected blocks beat a same-size generic memory by 4.5 points. This is the 'address selects parameters' design, and it uses zero context tokens. It is the strongest rival to 'address cues shared weights' on context-token economics.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: WISE: Rethinking the Knowledge Memory for Lifelong Model Editing of Large Language Models
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Lifelong writes go into a routed side memory; the activation router acts as an implicit address. This is a parameter-isolated alternative for which the question 'can the text be evicted?' has a different answer. Runnable in EasyEdit.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: ELDER: Enhancing Lifelong Model Editing with Mixture-of-LoRA
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: A routed mixture of LoRAs for lifelong edits. It is the same 'key selects a parameter block' family as hierarchical memories, and per-episode LoRA banks are its cheap analogue.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Memory Decoder: A Pretrained, Plug-and-Play Memory for Large Language Models
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Checked via search. A 0.5B decoder for the Qwen2.5 family is trained to imitate kNN-retriever distributions, so no datastore is needed at inference. This is whole-store eviction into a side network, the coarse-grained endpoint of the card's per-fact eviction. It is static (one domain), not sequential.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: MLP Memory: Language Modeling with Retriever-pretrained External Memory
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Same family as Memory Decoder: retriever behaviour is distilled into a parametric module that replaces the store. Cite with Memory Decoder.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Online Adaptation of Language Models with a Memory of Amortized Contexts
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: MAC stores a compact learned modulation per document and aggregates them at query time, with the base model frozen. Each store entry is compact and carries content, which is the latent alternative to an address that carries none. The plan's gist/Cartridges-style carrier is a cheaper stand-in.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Learning to Compress Prompts with Gist Tokens
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Survey-listed (working x latent) compressor. A compressed entry carries the content and does not depend on the weights. Cite it as the source of the compressed-entry baseline.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: In-Context Autoencoder for Context Compression in a Large Language Model
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Same compressed-entry family as gist tokens; supports the baseline at matched context tokens.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: R{\({^3}\)}Mem: Bridging Memory Retention and Retrieval via Reversible Compression
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: The title says it compresses stored context reversibly, so a compact entry can be expanded back to text. That is close to 'small entry, regenerate on demand', but here the compact entry carries the content; the card's address does not. Details not verified this session.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Memory${}^3$: Language Modeling with Explicit Memory
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Recalled from its abstract, not re-checked: it places knowledge in weights, explicit memory or RAG text according to cost. The address state is a further tier in that hierarchy (content in the weights, pointer in the store); cite it for the economics framing.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Pre-training Limited Memory Language Models with Internal and External Knowledge
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: The opposite pole: facts are kept out of the weights and always looked up. Dual-Layer is the other pole (facts only in the weights). The address state sits between the two.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Applies hippocampal indexing theory, but the index points to text passages. The card's index points into the weights, so it is the parametric counterpart.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: From RAG to Memory: Non-Parametric Continual Learning for Large Language Models
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: HippoRAG 2 argues for non-parametric continual learning: keep facts in the store. The card tests the hybrid position, where content lives in the weights and an index stays in the store.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Memory-R1: Enhancing Large Language Model Agents to Manage and Utilize Memories via Reinforcement Learning
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: A learned DELETE operation on a factual store. Its criterion is content-level, not whether the weights can still reach the fact, so the self-test gate is a new DELETE signal that could later become a reward.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Mem0: Building production-ready ai agents with scalable long-term memory
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: The ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP store operations that the card's reachability-gated demotion extends.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: LightMem: Lightweight and Efficient Memory-Augmented Generation
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Survey-listed compaction within the store (offline consolidation, with token-efficiency metrics). It is the store-to-store alternative to store-to-weights, next to Auto-Dreamer.

mapped.reframed_title: Keep the Index, Evict the Text: Reachability-Gated Forgetting for Facts Consolidated into a Small LM
mapped.reframed_one_liner: Each entity profile is fine-tuned into a <=1B LM. The store then demotes the entry from text to a short entity code that re-cues the copy in the weights, and moves the text to a cold archive only when a delayed, code-cued self-test passes. Scoring is accuracy at a fixed context-token budget on queries that need many entities (cross-episode 2-hop and aggregation). It is compared against a no-cue gate (Dual-Layer, i.e. standard consolidation), a LoRA bank selected by the same key (zero context tokens), SELF-PARAM writes and compressed-text entries.
changes: Reframe the contribution in survey terms. It is a cross-form forgetting operator: the token-level store's DELETE is conditioned on the state of the parametric store, which is the token-parametric sync gap the survey glosses over. Pitch it as a test of 7.1 (retrieval -> generation) and of index retention vs standard consolidation (7.8). Drop 'third store state' as the headline phrase.

Change the headline currency from hot-store bytes to context tokens. Storage was never the binding constraint: the big-picture doc's lesson 1, and 1,000 facts of text fit in kilobytes. Keep the evicted text in a cold archive that is not retrieved but can be restored. Report retention against context tokens per query as the main Pareto curve, with storage secondary.

Fix the unit of storage. A bioS atomic fact is about 10-15 tokens and the question already names the subject and relation, so a 4-token address saves at most about 3x, and the NL stub is nearly the question itself. Make the per-entity entry the headline (one code per person, cueing a 4-8 attribute profile of about 80-150 tokens), with per-fact and per-episode as ablations. Only then is a 10x context saving plausible.

Add queries where the context budget actually binds. With unique invented names and an oracle or BM25 entity lookup, single-hop questions are answered by top-1 full text in 256 tokens, so addresses buy nothing. Add cross-episode 2-hop, 3-hop and set/aggregation questions (e.g. 'which of these 30 people work in city X?') that need many entries in context; 4-token codes fit about 60 entities where full profiles fit 2-3. Pre-register that the address advantage appears only on these queries.

Redefine 'hidden' facts. With the full text in context, even the base model can answer by copying, so 'fails with no cue, passes with full text' does not pick out facts hidden in the weights. Define hidden as: answered with no cue right after its write, fails with no cue at episode t, and still keeps >=50% of its write-time log-prob gain on the answer (O'Neill's trace measure). Keep full text only as the ceiling in R, and subtract the never-trained-base-model + address control.

Demote the NL-stub arm to a control. A subject+relation stub duplicates the question, so it cannot separate addressing from template re-alignment, the confound O'Neill excluded. The primary arms become a random entity code (REMIX risk pre-registered) and a content-free NL handle (an invented nickname that is not inferable from the question). The stub joins the format-prime controls.

Add the parameter-isolation rival that the survey's factual-parametric cell implies: a per-episode (or per-entity-cluster) LoRA bank selected by the store's own retrieval key, a cheap analogue of hierarchical memories, ELDER and WISE. It uses zero context tokens. Pre-registered prediction: isolation wins direct recall per context token, and the shared-weight + address design wins cross-episode 2-hop composition. If the LoRA bank also wins 2-hop, demote the card to Tier B or fold it into #9.

Add SELF-PARAM-style KL context integration as a second write operator next to SFT. If SELF-PARAM writes leave facts reachable without a cue as well as SFT + address does, the address state is unnecessary and the work reduces to a Dual-Layer-style no-cue gate. Make this an explicit kill condition at the 0.6B pilot.

Make the gate comparison a test of the consolidation hypothesis. Track the fraction of facts that pass with the cue but fail without it, as a function of delay d (0, 1, 3, 6 episodes), number of later writes and restatement count. If it decays to about 0 with more restatements, the standard consolidation model holds, the address is only transient scaffolding, and the paper becomes a timing result for the no-cue gate.

Handle updating explicitly. For the 10% overwritten facts, measure the stale-value ('ghost') rate under the address cue, and add an invalidation rule: re-test the address after any same-entity write and restore the text on failure. This reuses card #1's ghost metric and the survey's updating operator.

Report trust metrics: the share of answers with no supporting text in the hot store (provenance loss), redirection under cue as confident hallucination, and a note that evicting text does not unlearn the fact.

Cut compute to about 80-100 GPU-h. Run the pilot and main grid on Qwen3-0.6B-Base, to match O'Neill, and Qwen2.5-0.5B. Run Qwen2.5-1.5B only for the final headline row, and Llama-3.2-1B with a single seed. Drop the EvolvingQA and kaist fictional-knowledge arms unless the pilot is GO. Replace the GCG suffix with a soft prompt trained on a disjoint fact set. Treat Memory Decoder as an optional single endpoint row.

Share logs with Arc 2. The per-fact cued and no-cue recall trajectories logged here are exactly the 'expiry' and 'reachability' signals that #9's rent/buy policy needs, so run #3's logging first and reuse it in #9's simulator.

mapped.rationale: The survey places #3 at a junction it barely covers. Factual token-level is dense (84), but the move from token-level to parametric followed by store pruning has no listed paper, and the survey (per third-party notes) glosses over keeping weights and store in sync. Frontiers 7.1 (retrieval -> generation), 7.2 (automated management) and 7.8 (indexing vs consolidation) frame the card more cleanly than its current 'third store state' pitch. The sparse cell is misleading, though. Dual-Layer and EVAF post-date the list. The survey's factual-parametric cell also surfaces a rival the card ignores: blocks of parameters selected by an address (hierarchical memories, where context-fetched blocks beat a generic memory by 4.5 points; WISE; ELDER; Memory Decoder for the whole store). That rival uses zero context tokens and threatens the economics claim. SELF-PARAM is a better write operator that may make the address unnecessary. Reading the card against the survey also exposed three design flaws. Atomic facts are too short for real token savings. The NL stub duplicates the question. 'Passes with full text' does not identify facts hidden in the weights. With the changes, the remaining claim is narrower but defensible: an index into shared weights buys multi-entity composition at low context cost, which neither isolation nor no-cue consolidation provides. Keep it in Tier A as the third pilot. If the key-selected LoRA bank matches it on cross-episode 2-hop, or SELF-PARAM writes close the cued vs no-cue gap, demote it to Tier B and fold it into #9. Search checks this session (snippets only): SELF-PARAM (arxiv.org/abs/2410.00487), hierarchical memories (arxiv.org/pdf/2510.02375), Memory Decoder (arxiv.org/html/2508.09874v1). R3Mem, Memory^3, LMLM and LightMem details are recalled, not verified.

mapped.survey_form: cross-form (token-level -> latent): a flat 1D buffer of raw keyframes (explicit, discrete, editable) is re-written into CUT3R/TTT3R's 768 latent state tokens. In the cached-ViT-token variant it is latent -> latent.
mapped.survey_function: working. The state is a capacity-limited scratchpad for one session. The experiment asks whether rehearsal alone lets this working store behave like long-term environment (factual) memory without adding a separate store.
dynamics_ops: evolution:consolidation (rehearsal: a buffered keyframe is re-written into the state with a beta-scaled write)
evolution:forgetting (pushes back against overwrite-driven forgetting; a forgetting signal sets the replay rate)
retrieval:timing (when to spend a pass on replay instead of a new frame; forgetting-triggered rho)
retrieval:query construction (which keyframe: anchor, co-visibility, maximal discrepancy)
retrieval:post-retrieval processing (beta write scaling; the pose memory is frozen during replays)
formation:latent representation (old frames are re-encoded into the state instead of read into context)
mapped.cell_density: Working x Latent is dense: 22 listed works, the densest latent cell. Nearly all of them are about what to drop or compress (H2O, SnapKV, Scissorhands, RazorAttention, Gist, ICAE) or are learned memory architectures (Titans, LM2, MemoRAG). The vision entries are XMem, MemoryVLA and VisMem. The cell has zero 3D-reconstruction entries, and no listed work does the card's operation: re-writing old observations into a fixed-size latent state under a compute budget. The source cell, Working x Token-level, has 14 works.
frontier_links: 7.2 Automated memory management: the forgetting-triggered replay rate is a closed-loop controller that needs no ground truth and no training, a cheap step from fixed heuristics toward policy-driven management

7.8 Human-cognitive connections: in Atkinson-Shiffrin terms, frame replay is maintenance rehearsal, the control process that keeps an item alive in the short-term store. The survey's listed vision precedent, XMem, copies the A-S stores but reads its buffer only by attention, which is the beta=0 analogue. The rehearsal reading is this project's interpretation; the survey does not say it.
Multimodal memory for embodied agents [ABS]: a perceptual 3D working memory, a form that is absent from the survey's list
Memory for world models [SEC]: the reconstructor's state is an online scene model. 'Context as Memory' is the nearest listed neighbour of this kind.
Survey critique on latency and engineering cost [SEC]: the paper's x-axis is forward passes per second, an explicit compute budget that the F/E/R taxonomy does not account for
Survey critique on complexity bias [SEC]: the oracle-tuned frame stride is exactly the simple brute-force baseline the critique says the survey undervalues
7.3 RL meets memory (learn when to recall or consolidate): answered here without training. RL is deliberately out of scope for budget reasons.
mapped.survey_claim_tested: Section 3 position [SNIP]: short-term and long-term memory 'emerge from the temporal patterns with which formation, evolution and retrieval are engaged', not from separate architectural modules. The test changes only the engagement schedule of one fixed 768-token latent state (replay fraction rho, write scale beta) at equal passes, and measures the state's effective memory horizon H with read-only probes. H is the lag at which a past keyframe's probe pose or depth error doubles. The position is confirmed if H(rho=25%) is at least 10x H(rho=0) (about 3 frames per AFG) on exploration sequences. It is falsified for capacity-bound latent working memory if H stays within 2x of H(rho=0) for every rho and beta; a separate store (#2 bank, #7 weights) would then be required. Related: F, E and R 'need not be invoked at every time step'; the card is the first compute-budgeted allocation between them. The wording comes from a search snippet, so verify it in the PDF.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Context as Memory: Scene-Consistent Interactive Long Video Generation with Memory Retrieval.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: It retrieves past frames by camera FOV overlap with the target view and concatenates them as context (confirmed by search). This is the card's 'coverage-near' selection rule, so attribute that rule to it. Two differences: it reads frames as conditioning context for generation and never writes them into a recurrent state, and it gets its poses from the user rather than predicting them. Search results also show 2026 follow-ups criticising FOV overlap as occlusion-blind ('MemLearner', 'Retrieve What's Missing').

survey_listed_overlaps.title: XMem: Long-Term Video Object Segmentation with an Atkinson-Shiffrin Memory Model.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: The closest listed precedent for 'recurrent state + frame buffer' in streaming vision: a per-frame recurrent sensory memory, a buffer of every r-th frame as working memory, and consolidation into long-term memory. It reads its buffer by attention, the beta=0 analogue, and never re-writes old frames into the recurrent state or matches compute. Use it for framing, not as a baseline.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: It keeps the first tokens permanently as attention sinks; the survey files it under Working x Parametric. It is the LLM source of the card's 'anchor (frame 0)' replay policy. The anchor-vs-recent contrast then tests whether frame 0 plays a sink or gauge role in a recurrent 3D state, against LongStream's and Anchor3R's claim that first-frame anchoring causes drift.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: IterResearch: Rethinking Long-Horizon Agents via Markovian State Reconstruction.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: It periodically discards the working context and rebuilds a compact workspace from an evolving report (confirmed by search). The 3D analogue is reset-and-rebuild: reset the state, then re-feed a few buffered keyframes. That is a pass-matched competitor to interleaved replay, and the card does not include it.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: The same family as the CUT3R/TTT3R fast state: a test-time-learned memory with surprise-scaled writes and decay. It never re-presents old inputs, so beta-scaled rehearsal is a term this family lacks. Conceptual only; it is not a 3D baseline.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: MEM1: Learning to Synergize Memory and Reasoning for Efficient Long-Horizon Agents.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: A constant-size internal state overwritten at every step has the same failure mode as CUT3R's state. MEM1 learns with RL what to keep; the card is the training-free alternative that changes the write schedule. Conceptual.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: MemAgent: Reshaping Long-Context LLM with Multi-Conv RL-based Memory Agent.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: A fixed-length overwrite memory updated chunk by chunk and trained with RL; same overwrite bottleneck as above, and conceptual only.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: MemoryVLA: Perceptual-Cognitive Memory in Vision-Language-Action Models for Robotic Manipulation.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: A latent perceptual memory bank for embodied control with retrieval and merge-style consolidation. Retrieval is read-only and there is no compute budget, so the overlap is weak. Cite it as the embodied neighbour in Working x Latent.

mapped.reframed_title: Rehearse or Advance? Can Pass-Budgeted Rehearsal Turn a 3-Frame Recurrent 3D State into Scene Memory?
mapped.reframed_one_liner: At a fixed number of forward passes per second, a training-free scheduler spends 5-25% of passes re-writing buffered keyframes into CUT3R/TTT3R's latent state. The paper reports two results: an equal-pass ATE frontier against stride, gating, reset-and-rebuild and the 2026 update rules, and the state's effective memory horizon as a function of replay fraction. The horizon result directly tests the survey's claim that long-term memory comes from how often formation and evolution run, not from a separate module.
changes: Make the headline two-part and pre-register it. (a) An equal-pass ATE frontier on exploration sequences. (b) The effective memory horizon H(rho, beta), measured by read-only probes on 20 past keyframes per sequence at lags 1-512. Confirm the survey position if H(25%) >= 10x H(0); falsify it if H stays within 2x for all rho and beta. Either way the result is publishable, which removes the card's main all-or-nothing risk. Fold #13's forgetting-curve probes in as this measurement section, as card #13 already suggests.

Add a pass-matched reset-and-rebuild baseline, the 3D analogue of IterResearch's Markovian state reconstruction. Every T in {50, 100, 200} frames, do a TTT3R reset, then spend k in {2, 4, 8} passes re-feeding co-visible buffered keyframes. Add a kill clause: if reset-and-rebuild comes within 3% ATE of interleaved replay on exploration sequences, the contribution reduces to a reset policy, which TTT3R and Info3R already own, so demote the work to the diagnostic paper.

Attribute each selection rule to its source and shrink the grid to four policies. Anchor comes from StreamingLLM's attention sinks. Coverage-near comes from Context as Memory's FOV-overlap retrieval. Discrepancy-max is MIR-style, using each keyframe's last measured gap between stored and re-predicted pose. Round-robin stays as the uniform control. Drop reservoir and coverage-far from the main grid.

Replace FOV-only co-visibility with geometry-verified co-visibility. Reproject each stored keyframe's predicted pointmap into the current predicted camera and z-test it against the current predicted depth; this needs no extra passes. This answers the occlusion critique of FOV retrieval found in search ('MemLearner', 'Retrieve What's Missing') and is a small new piece of its own.

Write the method in F/E/R terms. Each pass is either Formation on a new frame or Evolution (consolidation) of an old one. R covers timing (forgetting-triggered rho), the query (co-visibility) and post-retrieval processing (beta scaling and the pose-memory freeze). Claim the first compute-budgeted F-vs-E allocation, which fills the survey's admitted gap on latency and cost; do not claim replay as a new operator.

State the limits of the novelty honestly in the paper. In context-window models, retrieval re-reads the past at no write cost, and JRT re-reads for recurrent LMs (the card's own dropped-ideas table lists it). The 3D novelty therefore rests on the fact that a fixed recurrent state cannot retrieve without re-writing. Report the cached-token variant (latent -> latent) against the image-buffer variant (token -> latent) under FLOP-matched accounting.

Share one within-session comparison table with #2, covering three ways to bring back the past at equal passes: restore a snapshot from a latent repository (#2), reset and rebuild from the raw buffer, and interleaved rehearsal (#4). This turns Arc 1 chapters 1-2 into a single store-comparison story, and both cards reuse the same TTT3R hooks.

Cut cost from about 150 to about 100 GPU-h. Run every sweep on cut3r_224_linear_4 and use the 512 checkpoint only for frontier endpoints. Drop the Point3R contrast and the video-depth sets (Bonn, KITTI depth) from the main paper. Keep ATE on ScanNet, TUM and KITTI plus 7-Scenes Acc/Comp. Stack replay only on TTT3R, ReCal3R and TTSA3R; AFG and Info3R remain baselines.

Pilot changes, about 10 GPU-h instead of 8. Add H(rho) probes for rho in {0, 10, 25}% on the 16 pilot sequences, plus 4 reset-and-rebuild configurations. Keep the existing three-part GO rule and add the reset-and-rebuild kill clause.

Context-as-Memory-style FOV-overlap selection as the coverage-near policy, compared with geometry-verified co-visibility from CUT3R's own pointmaps
StreamingLLM-style frame-0 'sink' anchor replay as the attributed anchor policy
MIR-style maximal-discrepancy replay selection (MIR is already cited in the project's own files), using each keyframe's last stored-vs-re-predicted pose gap
#2's snapshot restore at equal passes, sharing one within-session table
mapped.rationale: The survey does not weaken the card's novelty in its niche, because it lists no streaming 3D reconstruction work at all. It does not strengthen the evidence either: it offers no runnable baselines, and the card's real competitors (oracle-tuned stride, AFG, Info3R, TTSA3R, ReCal3R, Anchor3R) all sit outside it. The main risk is unchanged: replay may be only a smarter stride, in a field of about 7 training-free update-rule papers in 2026. The survey also shows the conceptual novelty is narrower than the card implies. Re-injecting the past into working memory is routine in token-level and KV systems, and Context as Memory already selects past frames by FOV overlap. The genuinely new part is the write: re-writing old observations into a fixed latent state under a pass budget, for which the dense Working x Latent cell (22 works, mostly eviction and compression) has no entry. The survey's real contribution here is a better scientific question. The Section 3 claim that short-term vs long-term memory comes from the temporal pattern of F/E/R gives the card a pre-registrable test, the memory horizon as a function of replay fraction, that is publishable whether it confirms or falsifies the claim. The survey's listed IterResearch also points to a missing pass-matched competitor, reset-and-rebuild, which raises the bar and could kill the method claim early. Both changes, plus the scope cuts, make the card sharper and cheaper, at about 100 GPU-h for the paper and about 10 GPU-h for the pilot, but they do not move it above Tier B. Keep it as the second chapter of Arc 1, with #13's probes folded in.

mapped.rationale: The survey helps #5's positioning but weakens its headline. Positioning: the survey's list has no work on consolidating a test-time-written latent working state into persistent weights inside one model; Nested Learning/HOPE is not listed at all. The survey also states a claim #5 can test directly: short- and long-term memory emerge from temporal patterns of formation, evolution and retrieval. Headline: the survey's own Titans entry is HOPE's fast component, and Titans already has a data-dependent forget gate plus momentum, which act as retention asymmetry and an implicit extra timescale (Jones et al.). Real HOPE therefore probably escapes the lagged-copy degeneracy by design. As written, the card's claim that HOPE CMS levels are lagged copies is likely wrong for the full architecture. Recasting the work as a forgetting-by-frequency factorial plus an attribution ablation keeps the result informative either way. It is cheaper (about 40-60 GPU-h), and it puts the contribution in the survey's vocabulary: the schedule of formation is not a timescale, while asymmetric forgetting is, and consolidation and forgetting cannot be separated under a shared loss. The underlying principle is still prior art (Jones 2023, Smith 2006, Hinton & Plaut 1987). The contribution is an operational test, a design rule and an attribution, so the card stays Tier B and is not a lead paper. Search checks: Titans' decay gate and momentum (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.00663, https://arxiv.org/html/2501.00663v1); M+ writing dropped short-term tokens to a long-term store (https://arxiv.org/html/2502.00592v2, https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/wang25au.html); Memoria's three-store engram design, whose lifespan rules were unconfirmed (https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.03052v3, https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/park24a.html). mapped.reframed_title: Where Does Forgetting Live in Experience Memory? Attributing Backward-Transfer Loss to Formation, Evolution and Retrieval in Token-Level Agent Memory
mapped.reframed_one_liner: A training-free study on the ALFWorld/BabyAI experience-reuse stream. Counterfactual oracles split BWT into four parts: displacement at retrieval, collisions from key formation, loss from consolidation, and reader failure. It also tests whether strategy-level abstraction buys forward transfer at the cost of collision density. Margin-gated contrastive key rewriting is one arm among several, pitted against MemRL utility re-ranking and ExpeL/AWM-style group consolidation at equal tokens.
changes: Reframe the contribution from a method paper to an operator-attribution study. Run four counterfactual oracles on the same logged stream. (a) R-displacement oracle: the existing one, which removes newer same-group competitors. (b) R-utility oracle: rank candidates by true single-slot utility. (c) E-consolidation oracle: merge each collision group into one LLM-written procedure. (d) Reader oracle: force the helpful entry into context and measure residual failure, i.e. negative transfer from the reader. Report a BWT decomposition table. This table is the paper's main result, and the method arms are secondary.

Add an abstraction axis that matches the survey's case -> strategy spectrum. For case-based values (raw trajectories) vs strategy-based values (abstract procedures), and fine vs coarse keys, measure key-space collision density (fraction of pairs above tau_c), Displacement Rate, FWT and BWT. Hypothesis H0: the FWT/BWT trade-off that 2604.27003 reports across configurations is mediated by collision density. Test it with a simple mediation fit across configurations and embedders.

Make MemRL two-phase retrieval (semantic recall then Q-utility re-ranking) the primary baseline. Rewrite GO condition 3 so the method must beat MemRL and ExpeL/AWM-style group consolidation by >=3 BWT points at equal context tokens, not only MMR/xMemory. If MemRL alone recovers >=70% of the oracle headroom, drop the rewrite method and publish the attribution study with 'utility re-ranking fixes R-side forgetting' as a finding.

Close the cap-artifact hole. With only 6 ALFWorld task types, a de-duplicated distilled store may fit fully in context. Sweep k in {1, 3, 5, all} and store size, report the context-fit threshold where displacement disappears, and include an ACE-style full-playbook baseline. To keep the store much larger than k, lengthen the stream (many entries per task type, BabyAI levels as a second stream), rather than relying on the cap alone.

Replace the extra-rollout 'helpful entry' labelling with running MemRL-style Q-values or success attribution logged during the stream. Validate this proxy against leave-one-in rollouts on a small calibration subset (about 50 queries). This cuts API cost and reuses the baseline's machinery.

Drop the LongMemEval/Entity-Collision conversational track completely. It sits in the factual x token-level cell, which MemStrata, Entity-Collision and MINTEval already cover. Dropping it saves the GPT-4o judge budget and keeps the paper inside one survey cell.

Keep the Crowded Embedding Space self-relevance foil (A-MEM-style key evolution vs contrastive rewriting). It stays as the one result that still pays off if the method is only moderate, since it is a theory test inside a real agent loop.

Rewrite related work and the novelty verdict. The card's closest-work list omits every survey-listed ALFWorld experience-memory system: MemRL, Memp, ExpeL, and H2R if confirmed. Name MemRL as prior art for read-side stability-plasticity management. The remaining novelty is the per-operator attribution and the abstraction-collision mediation, not 'first management method'.
Use the Memp codebase as a fallback harness if the 2604.27003 protocol does not reproduce in week 1, and MemRL's released code for the main baseline. Keep the gpt-4o-mini backbone, pinned and cached.

State the claim in survey terms in the abstract. Forgetting in token-level experiential memory comes from the F-R interaction (appending at F reorders R for old queries), not from a deliberate E-forgetting operator. The paper locates which operator carries it and which fix works where.

Expected cost after the changes: about 10-15 GPU-hours (embedders/reranker only) plus $80-150 API. That is cheaper than the current ~30 GPU-hours plus up to $150, because the conversational track and most utility-labelling rollouts are gone.

mapped.rationale: The survey list shows the card's gap is narrower than stated. The cell (experiential x token-level, 46 works) is dense. In it, MemRL already tackles the read-side competition between old and new experiences on a frozen LLM, evaluates on ALFWorld and Lifelong Agent Bench, and explicitly claims to resolve stability-plasticity. Memp already studies key construction and update policies for procedural memory on ALFWorld. ReMe already adds scenario-aware indexing and utility pruning against append-only memory. ExpeL, AWM and ACE give consolidation and de-dup routes that the card never benchmarks. So margin-gated contrastive key rewriting is one more write/read heuristic in a crowded cell, and with only 6 ALFWorld task types the k=3 displacement may partly be an artifact of the cap. The defensible and survey-relevant core is the measurement, and it is cheap. It means splitting backward-transfer loss across the F/E/R operators with counterfactual oracles, and testing two positions: that token-level memory sidesteps forgetting, and that strategy-level abstraction transfers at no cost. Demote it from method paper to Tier C diagnostic and reframe it as above. It remains a sensible cheap side project in the external-store-hygiene arc. Optionally, share the harness with #15, whose rewrite-rot result would supply the E-side arm of the attribution table. Third-party critiques [SEC]: the complexity bias toward undervaluing brute-force baselines argues for adding a plain explicit-map arm. The point about keeping parametric and token stores in sync maps to changed-scene staleness, which stays deferred for budget.
mapped.survey_claim_tested: Primary: the survey's position [SNIP] that short-term vs long-term memory 'emerge from the temporal patterns with which formation, evolution and retrieval are engaged', not from separate architectural modules. S1/S2 turn the working-memory module into long-term memory just by persisting it; S4/S6 move the content into a separate parametric module. If a persisted snapshot matches the adapter at every first-visit length L, that supports the position in a non-LLM system. If a capacity crossover appears (weights win only once L exceeds state capacity), it qualifies the position: long-term memory needs a change of form once working-memory capacity is exceeded. Secondary: the qualitative form trade-off [SEC]: token-level stores dominate in practice; parametric memory is efficient but forgetting-prone; latent memory is efficient but opaque. #7 can turn this into a matched-byte, single-task measurement across all three forms.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Self-Updatable Large Language Models by Integrating Context into Model Parameters.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Same objective in LLMs (search-verified): a copy of the model without the context is trained to match the with-context model's outputs (KL), with no added parameters. S4 (full-A teacher -> reset-state sub-clip student) is its 3D analogue. Credit it as the conceptual precedent for state -> weights distillation.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Online Adaptation of Language Models with a Memory of Amortized Contexts.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: MAC (search-verified) amortizes each document into a compact PEFT modulation in one forward pass, stores the modulations in a memory bank, and aggregates them per query for a frozen LM, with no test-time gradients. The CUT3R snapshot (S2) is an amortized context in exactly this sense, so S2 vs S4 is the 3D instance of amortized vs per-context optimized memory. Adopt this framing, and treat MAC's efficiency claim as a hypothesis to test.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Pretraining with hierarchical memories: separating long-tail and common knowledge.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: The backbone holds common knowledge while a context-fetched parametric bank holds the long tail. This frames a per-scene adapter library fetched by place descriptor: scene geometry is long-tail knowledge, and the CUT3R prior is common knowledge.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: MemLoRA: Distilling Expert Adapters for On-Device Memory Systems.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Distilled adapters used as memory. A precedent for S4's 'adapter as stored memory item', to cite in related work.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: K-Adapter: Infusing Knowledge into Pre-Trained Models with Adapters.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Knowledge-specific adapters on a frozen backbone. The same frozen-backbone + per-knowledge-adapter design as S4.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Memory Decoder: A Pretrained, Plug-and-Play Memory for Large Language Models.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: A separate plug-in parametric memory module beside a frozen model. The analogue of S6, the ACE-style scene-coordinate head on frozen CUT3R features.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: WISE: Rethinking the Knowledge Memory for Lifelong Model Editing of Large Language Models.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Side memory with a router deciding when to use it. Its routing failure mode is H5 (wrong-scene adapter harm); report routing accuracy alongside harm.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: ELDER: Enhancing Lifelong Model Editing with Mixture-of-LoRA.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: A mixture of LoRAs accumulated over a lifelong stream. The analogue of the missing arm: one shared or mixed adapter across many scenes rather than isolated per-scene adapters.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: XMem: Long-Term Video Object Segmentation with an Atkinson-Shiffrin Memory Model.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: The closest vision precedent for working -> long-term consolidation inside a video stream, in latent form (prototype consolidation). It suggests a training-free consolidated-snapshot variant of S2.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: M+: Extending MemoryLLM with Scalable Long-Term Memory.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: A latent long-term repository with a retriever. The LLM analogue of a bank of CUT3R state snapshots (S2), which is card #2's mechanism.

survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: The only vision entry in factual-latent (search-verified): a VLM encodes knowledge into 8 continuous embeddings. A precedent for compact latent memory for visual models, and the analogue of a compressed snapshot.

survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: An embodied latent memory bank. A neighbour in working-latent to cite, not a runnable baseline.

mapped.reframed_title: Keep the state, or change its form? A matched-byte test of latent, token and parametric scene memory for CUT3R revisits (phase 2 of #2)
mapped.reframed_one_liner: On #2's revisit pairs, ask which memory form a scene should take when a frozen CUT3R's working state must become long-term: a persisted latent snapshot (amortized formation, MAC-style), raw or structured tokens (keyframes, an explicit downsampled map), or parameters (an LN/LoRA adapter or SCR head; optimized formation). Measure at matched bytes and on a formation-seconds axis. This tests the survey's claim that long-term memory is a matter of dynamics, not of a separate module. Also test whether a ground-truth-free trigger predicts when a change of form pays off.
changes: Hypothesis: restate H1 in survey terms as 'the winning form changes with first-visit length L'. Pre-register three outcomes: (a) snapshot >= adapter at all L supports the survey's 'long-term emerges from dynamics, not modules'; (b) a crossover where weights win only beyond state capacity qualifies it; (c) a token-level/explicit map wins A-anchored registration at all L, which confirms the [SEC] 'token-level dominates in practice' observation. Set equivalence margins (e.g. +/-2% relative ATE) up front so outcome (a) or (c) is a publishable result, not a failed go/no-go.

Add the missing brute-force token-level arm S7, motivated by the survey critique about complexity bias: A's fused pointmap downsampled to ~1.5-2 MB (about 150-250k fp16 points with confidence) plus global descriptors of the stored keyframes. B's first frames are registered by ICP/PnP of CUT3R's own pointmaps against it. Reuse #2's MASt3R+PnP code. Also add a byte-allocation variant of S3: K=8 keyframes at 512 px vs K=32 at 224 px at equal bytes.

Correct the consolidation claim: a library of isolated per-scene adapters has no cross-scene interference, so it is an external store whose entries happen to be weights, not consolidation in the continual-learning sense. Add one shared LN/bias-only adapter updated sequentially over A plus the G in {0,3} interfering scenes, with and without keyframe replay, and report how much of scene A it forgets. This is the only arm where the survey's 'parametric memory suffers catastrophic forgetting' trade-off can appear (an ELDER-style mixture is the optional upgrade).

Replace the single <=60 s budget with a formation-cost frontier, following MAC's amortized vs optimized framing: plot revisit quality against formation seconds in {0 (snapshot), 10, 30, 60, 120} and against bytes. Report S2 as amortized formation and S4/S6 as optimized formation.

Make A-anchored relocalization primary (recall at 25 cm/10 deg on B's first 20 frames, plus A-anchored ATE), matching #2's metric, and keep B-self ATE/Acc secondary. Free Geometry's ~3-4% gains mean B-self differences will likely sit inside the CIs at 14 pairs.

Cut cost from ~160 to ~60-80 GPU-h. In the pilot use only an LN/bias adapter trained on 4-frame sub-clips at 224-384 px, and the SCR head on cached frozen encoder features (no BPTT). Escalate to a rank-4 decoder LoRA at 512 px only if LN-only gives >=3% on the primary metric. Drop ScanNet rescans and 12-Scenes from the first version; use 7-Scenes for fitting and TUM for the held-out policy test.

Recast the earned signal as a formation trigger (survey 7.2). Keep F vs L-only vs the TTT3R learning-rate statistic, and add a 3-feature logistic policy (F, 20-step distillability, LR statistic) fit on 7-Scenes and tested on TUM, scored by regret against always-form, never-form and the per-cell oracle. Do not claim RL or a learned management policy beyond this.

Report wrong-route harm per form (snapshot, adapter, SCR head, explicit map), with routing accuracy of the place descriptor as in WISE-style routing, to show which form fails most safely (survey trustworthy-memory frontier). Many failures may be routing errors, not consolidation errors, so log them separately.

Optional, training-free and cheap: an XMem-style consolidated latent store, i.e. 2-4 snapshots taken across A, quantized to int8 to stay within the byte budget, and retrieved by B's first frame. This tests whether the latent form fails because of capacity or because of recency (the end-of-A snapshot forgets early A).

Structure: run this as phase 2 of #2 on the same revisit pairs and fork, reusing S1-S3 and verify-before-restore. #7's unique content becomes S4/S5/S6/S7, the shared-adapter interference arm, the formation-cost frontier and the formation trigger. Framing: '#2 shows the state is worth keeping; this phase asks what form it should be kept in.'
added_baselines: S7 explicit structured map: A's fused pointmap downsampled to ~2 MB + keyframe global descriptors, B registered by ICP/PnP (reuses #2's MASt3R+PnP pipeline)
Byte-allocation keyframe variant: K=32 at 224 px vs K=8 at 512 px at equal bytes
Shared sequential LN/bias adapter across A + G interfering scenes, with and without keyframe replay (the true consolidation arm, exposing interference)
XMem-style consolidated latent store: 2-4 int8 snapshots across A retrieved by B's first frame (training-free)
Formation-seconds sweep {0,10,30,60,120} for S4/S6 against S2 at 0 s (MAC-style amortized vs optimized comparison)
3-feature logistic formation policy vs F-threshold vs L-only vs TTT3R LR statistic, with regret to always/never/oracle
mapped.rationale: Through the survey's lens #7 has a sharper purpose than the card states. It is the only shortlisted idea that puts all three of the survey's forms (latent, token, parametric) on one task at matched bytes. It can test a specific survey position: that short- and long-term memory differ by F/E/R dynamics rather than by module. It also fills the survey's total absence of streaming 3D reconstruction. But the survey also makes the card's weaknesses plainer. (1) The empty vision/3D corner of factual-parametric reflects the survey's LLM scope, not open ground: Free Geometry, LoRA3D and ACE-G already own the mechanisms. On the LLM side, 'Self-Updatable LLMs...' (KL from with-context to no-context model) and MAC (amortized context modulations in a bank) already pose the same latent -> parametric and amortized-vs-optimized questions. (2) Per-scene adapters avoid interference, so the card's 'consolidation into weights' is really an external store of weight deltas; true consolidation, with forgetting, is untested unless a shared-adapter arm is added. (3) The survey's own observation that token-level stores dominate in practice, plus its complexity-bias critique, predicts that a plain explicit map or keyframe store will win the registration metric. Meanwhile the adapter's expected B-self gain (~3-4%) is within noise at 14 pairs. (4) At ~160 GPU-h with BPTT through CUT3R it is the most expensive card in Arc 1, and its S1-S3 arms are #2's mechanisms. The judge already recommended running it as phase 2 of #2. Merging it into #2 as the 'which form should a kept scene take' phase, at ~60-80 GPU-h with the brute-force map arm, the shared-adapter interference arm and pre-registered equivalence margins, keeps the survey-level contribution and drops the standalone-benchmark risk. Search checks (3 used): MAC mechanism confirmed (arxiv.org/abs/2403.04317); SELF-PARAM's KL with-context -> without-context objective confirmed (arxiv.org/abs/2410.00487); CoMEM confirmed as 8-embedding continuous memory for VLMs, not 3D (arxiv.org/abs/2505.17670).

mapped.survey_form: token-level: an experiential text store gated against the backbone's own parametric competence, since 'no memory' means falling back on the weights; entries also move between case-level and strategy-level inside the cell
mapped.survey_function: experiential: strategy-based (cheatsheet, playbook or insight bank), with raw case-based episodes as the fallback store
dynamics_ops: retrieval:timing/intent: decide per query whether R is invoked at all; abstaining defers to the parametric no-memory answer
evolution:forgetting: demote an entry from strategy level to case level using paired win/loss audit evidence
evolution:consolidation: the anchor-NLL write gate (recommended for cutting to an appendix)
formation:semantic summarization: gated promotion of raw episodes into strategy-level insights
mapped.cell_density: Dense. Experiential x token-level holds 46 works in the survey's list, the second-densest cell after factual x token-level (84). It is dense in builders (DC, ACE, ReasoningBank, ExpeL, ReMe, MemRL, FLEX, Training-Free GRPO, Buffer of Thoughts) and in heuristic or learned management. None of the 46 offers a non-regression guarantee or measures harm against a no-memory policy, so the guarantee niche itself is empty.
frontier_links: Trustworthy memory: the survey frames trust as privacy, explainability and robustness to leakage and hallucination. #8 adds 'performance no worse than no memory' as a measurable, certifiable trust criterion.

7.2 Automated memory management: the survey sees a move from handcrafted heuristics to learned, policy-driven pipelines. #8 offers a third route, statistically calibrated control with finite-sample (CRC) and long-run (ACI) guarantees, which can wrap either kind.

7.3 RL meets agent memory: Memory-R1, Mem-alpha and MemRL learn when to recall and what to keep. #8 asks whether those learned recall utilities hold a harm budget as memory drifts, and calibrates them if not.
Dynamics: the survey notes F, E and R 'need not be invoked at every time step'. #8 gives a certified rule for when R should not be invoked.
Third-party critique ([SEC]) that the survey undervalues simple brute-force baselines: #8 makes compute-matched no-memory self-consistency the reference policy that every memory system must beat.
mapped.survey_claim_tested: Primary: the 7.2/7.3 position that the way forward is learned, policy-driven memory management (Memory-R1, Mem-alpha, MemRL). Falsifiable form: a learned utility score such as MemRL's Q-values, thresholded as-is, exceeds a harm budget against no memory once the store drifts, while the same score wrapped in CRC/ACI stays within it. That would show learned managers need calibration, not only training. Secondary: the experiential-memory section's growing emphasis on strategy-based, transferable memory over case-based memory. Measuring paired harm at each abstraction level, at matched tokens, tests whether harm concentrates where the LLM abstracts (strategy level) rather than in raw case retrieval. 2605.12978's finding that Episodic-only regimes recover most of the gain predicts it does.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Dynamic Cheatsheet: Test-Time Learning with Adaptive Memory
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: The card's main builder and source of its streams (Game of 24, MATH, MMLU-Pro). DC-Cumulative's monolithic rewriting is where harm is expected to be largest.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: A builder already in the plan. ACE motivates itself with 'context collapse': as recalled, monolithic rewriting dropped accuracy below the no-adaptation baseline (verify exact numbers). That is a survey-listed precedent for the harm phenomenon beside 2605.12978. ACE's incremental delta updates are a write-side mitigation built into the builder, which competes directly with the anchor-NLL write gate and may shrink the harm the read gate has to control.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: MemRL: Self-Evolving Agents via Runtime Reinforcement Learning on Episodic Memory
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Closest listed read-side manager. It keeps the LLM frozen and uses two-phase retrieval: semantic filtering, then ranking by learned Q-value utilities updated from environment feedback (confirmed by search; code public). This overlaps the read gate's per-entry win-rate feature and the eviction rule. It has no guarantee and no paired no-memory reference, so it should be a score to wrap, not just a competitor.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Remember Me, Refine Me: A Dynamic Procedural Memory Framework for Experience-Driven Agent Evolution
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: ReMe's 'utility-based refinement' admits validated memories and prunes outdated ones (confirmed by search; the scoring details were not visible). It overlaps both the write gate (validated admission) and paired-evidence eviction. It is heuristic and has no harm bound.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: A hybrid case-plus-insight builder whose insight list is edited by add/edit/upvote/downvote importance counts. It is the heuristic precursor of #8's paired win/loss demotion, and a natural heuristic eviction baseline.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Buffer of Thoughts: Thought-Augmented Reasoning with Large Language Models
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: A strategy-based thought-template meta-buffer with a buffer manager, evaluated on Game of 24. It is a second strategy-level builder on the card's own stream.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: A strategy-based insight memory distilled from both successes and failures. The card already names a ReasoningBank-style memory as a stretch builder.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Memory-R1: Enhancing Large Language Model Agents to Manage and Utilize Memories via Reinforcement Learning
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: An RL-trained manager (ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP) plus an answer agent that filters retrieved memories before answering. That is learned read-side filtering with no guarantee. It is too costly to retrain under the GPU budget, so cite it as related work, not as a baseline.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: MemEvolve: Meta-Evolution of Agent Memory Systems
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Its EvolveLab codebase re-implements 12 memory systems behind an encode/store/retrieve/manage interface, with an online streaming mode (confirmed by search). The 'manage' slot (consolidation, abstraction, selective forgetting) is exactly where #8's gate and demotion would plug in. That makes it a candidate builder library. Its own benchmarks (GAIA, xBench, DeepResearchBench) are too costly and rely on judge grading, so builders should be ported to the verifiable streams.
