survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Targets retrieved context overriding the model's own knowledge (context-memory conflict), the same mechanism as #8's 'memory overrides existing competence' hypothesis. It is a trained, latent-form method: related work, not a baseline.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: FLEX: Continuous Agent Evolution via Forward Learning from Experience
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Claims that growing the experience library keeps improving performance. The card's paired harm-versus-stream-position curve directly checks such monotone-gain claims.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Unveiling Privacy Risks in LLM Agent Memory
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: The survey list's representative of trustworthy memory, on the privacy axis. #8 would add a performance non-regression axis to that frontier.

mapped.reframed_title: Certified retrieval timing: a do-no-harm guarantee for experiential text memory against the model's own competence
mapped.reframed_one_liner: A black-box calibration layer turns any memory-utility score (hand features, MemRL Q-values, ExpeL/ReMe-style counts) into a finite-sample (CRC) and online (ACI) guarantee. Injecting accumulated experiential text memory then breaks at most alpha of the problems the frozen model already solves on its own. An anytime-valid paired test demotes harmful insights from strategy level to case level, and a harm-budgeted gain metric ranks survey-listed builders against compute-matched no memory. Actors are API-only and the open-model ablation is at most 1.5B, for roughly 25-40 GPU-hours.
changes: Cut the anchor-NLL write gate from the main paper; leave a short appendix or drop it. It costs about 80 of the plan's 160 GPU-hours (anchor scoring 20, rollout labels 15, Janus/Recuris runs 10, write gate in the loop 35). It is also the least novel part: the survey list already has ACE (incremental delta updates) and ReMe (validated admission), and the card's own search found Janus, Recuris, AGMR and InfoMem. The paper should lead only with the paired read-side guarantee and the certified demotion.

Reframe in survey vocabulary as a certified retrieval-timing operator. The gate decides whether R is invoked, and abstaining hands the query to the backbone's parametric competence. Define the paired loss explicitly as 'experiential token memory overrides parametric competence', and cite Conflict-Aware Soft Prompting and MemTrim for the mechanism.

Make the guarantee a wrapper over any utility score, not a new score. Run (a) the card's logistic harm score on cheap features, (b) MemRL Q-values from its public code, (c) ExpeL/ReMe-style utility counts and (d) top retrieval cosine. Report each score twice: as a plug-in threshold, and wrapped in CRC (offline) and ACI (online). The headline result is 'same score, with versus without calibration, under memory drift', which tests the 7.2/7.3 position directly.

Go API-first. Use claude-haiku-5-5 as the main actor and gpt-5-mini as the second. Replace Qwen3-8B with Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (or Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B) as a capability ablation that supplies logprob features. Memory Trust Gap's capability-dependent harm predicts that small models show more harm and less gain, a useful stress test where the gate should abstain more. Target 25-40 GPU-hours in total.

Run the no-memory arm (k=3 samples plus one placebo draw) once per dataset item and cache it. It does not depend on the memory state, so builders, seeds and gate variants can all share it, and each extra builder costs only its memory arm. Use prompt caching for the shared memory prefix. Re-estimate API spend under this design before committing to 4 datasets x 4 builders x 3 seeds.

Add an abstraction axis that matches the survey's experiential spectrum: case-based (raw-episode top-k, the 'Episodic-only' regime), strategy-based (DC-Cumulative, ACE, Buffer of Thoughts) and hybrid (ExpeL). Report paired harm, harm net of the placebo floor and certified gain at each level at matched injected tokens. This is the measurement that tests the survey's strategy-over-case emphasis.

Turn eviction into a certified forgetting operator. Replace the ad hoc 'posterior P(harm > benefit) > 0.9' rule with an anytime-valid sequential test on each entry's paired win/loss stream (a confidence sequence or e-process), so false demotions stay controlled despite continuous monitoring. Demote from strategy level to the raw case store rather than delete. This is CPU-only.

Absorb Tier C card #15. Add its lineage depth (LLM rewrite passes from the raw episodes) as a harm-score feature beside 'rewrite count', and use depth-bounded regeneration from raw episodes as the target for demoted entries. Then park #15 as its own project.

Tighten the go/kill rule for builder generality. Require harm above the placebo floor on at least 2 builders, at least one of them not DC-Cumulative (ACE or raw-episode retrieval), or on the ARC replication with memory distilled from ground truth. If only DC-Cumulative shows harm, downgrade to a short note: ACE already addresses monolithic rewriting, so a gate that only fixes DC is weak.

Add a reusable evaluation contribution: 'harm-budgeted net gain', the accuracy over compute-matched sc@k no memory at certified harm <= alpha. Report it as a leaderboard over at least 4 survey-listed builders. This answers the critique that the survey undervalues brute-force baselines, and lasts beyond any single gate.

Validate offline replay against in-the-loop use on one stream. The plan lets memory evolve only from the memory arm. In deployment, abstained queries would feed no-memory trajectories back to the builder, so show that the offline CRC/ACI numbers match a gated run where that happens.

Cite ACE's 'context collapse' (survey-listed) next to 2605.12978 as prior evidence that memory can fall below the no-adaptation baseline. State the gap precisely: these works observe or mitigate the drop inside a builder, while #8 bounds it for any builder, black-box.

Remember Me, Refine Me: A Dynamic Procedural Memory Framework for Experience-Driven Agent Evolution (utility-based refinement as the eviction baseline)
ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners (hybrid builder; upvote/downvote insight importance as the heuristic demotion baseline)
Buffer of Thoughts: Thought-Augmented Reasoning with Large Language Models (strategy-level template builder on Game of 24)
mapped.rationale: In the survey's terms, #8 sits in the densest experiential cell (experiential x token-level, 46 works), but it targets an operator nobody there certifies. Many listed works build strategy-level memories, and some manage them by heuristics (ExpeL votes, ReMe utility refinement, ACE delta updates) or by learned utilities (MemRL, Memory-R1), but none bounds harm against the no-memory policy. The paired, black-box CRC/ACI read guarantee is therefore a real and well-positioned gap. It links to three survey frontiers (trustworthy memory, automated management, RL-managed memory) and gives a falsifiable test of the 7.2/7.3 claim that learned managers are the way forward. The survey also shows the card is weaker than it claims in two places. First, the write-gate half is crowded by survey-listed builders with built-in write-side fixes (ACE, ReMe) as well as Janus, Recuris, AGMR and InfoMem, and it consumes half the GPU budget. Second, the harm phenomenon has a survey-listed builder designed to prevent it (ACE), so harm may be specific to the builder. Rescoping to the read guarantee plus certified demotion fixes both, and moving to API actors with a <=1.5B ablation and a cached no-memory arm cuts compute from about 160 to about 25-40 GPU-hours. Requiring harm on a non-DC builder protects against the builder-specific risk. The idea stays secondary to the user's 3D and fact-lifecycle arcs, but after these changes it is one of the cheapest, cleanest papers on the shortlist. Sources checked with WebSearch: [MemRL](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.03192v1), [ReMe](https://arxiv.org/html/2512.10696v1), [MemEvolve](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.18746).

mapped.survey_form: cross-form (token-level -> parametric, with demotion back to token-level when a fact changes)
mapped.survey_function: factual (stays factual; the move is across forms, not across functions)
dynamics_ops: formation: parametric internalization (MEMIT/AlphaEdit/LoRA write of a stored fact)
evolution: consolidation (store -> weights at buy time)
evolution: updating (fact change expires the purchase; conflict between a stale weight copy and the retrieved new value)
evolution: forgetting (evict the store copy after buying; demote to retrieval-first after expiry)
retrieval: timing (a bought fact skips retrieval, so the policy also schedules when R is invoked)
mapped.cell_density: Source cell factual x token-level is dense (84 listed works). Target cell factual x parametric is moderately sparse (16) and is almost all editors or parametric modules: AlphaEdit, WISE, ELDER, MEND, MAC, Memory Decoder, MLP Memory. No listed work manages the online, post-deployment move of changing facts between these two cells. The closest listed works make a static split at pretraining time: Memory^3 (in factual x latent, 8 works), 'Pretraining with hierarchical memories' and LMLM.
frontier_links: 7.2 Automated memory management: replaces handcrafted write-back heuristics (LFU/LRU, periodic SFT) with a policy whose regret against a clairvoyant schedule can be analysed

7.3 RL meets agent memory ('learn ... how to consolidate'): offers a learning-augmented online algorithm with competitive bounds as a cheap, analysable alternative to RL-trained managers (Memory-R1, Mem-alpha); a CPU contextual-bandit policy in the simulator can stand in for the RL comparator
Trustworthy memory: stale answers from expired parametric copies are a hallucination source, and an irreversible weight write makes later deletion or unlearning harder than deleting a store entry
Survey blind spot flagged by a third-party critique ([SEC], less reliable): keeping a parametric copy synchronized with a token-level copy as both change. This card targets that gap directly
mapped.survey_claim_tested: Memory^3, which the survey lists, argues for a 'memory hierarchy': place frequently used knowledge in high-write-cost, low-read-cost forms (the weights) and rarely used knowledge in cheap-to-write, expensive-to-read forms (explicit memory, RAG). This was confirmed by search. The card can falsify frequency-only placement for changing facts. Its index is demand x rent x write-generalization / (change hazard x drift price), and it predicts that frequently queried but volatile facts (P6/P35 head of government, P54 sports team, P286 head coach) should stay in the token-level store. Frequency-only placement would put them in the weights. Secondary: the card can confirm the survey's position that short-term vs long-term memory 'emerge from the temporal patterns with which formation, evolution and retrieval are engaged'. Here a fact's parametric (long-term) status would emerge from its demand and hazard pattern, not from a fixed module.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Memory${}^3$: Language Modeling with Explicit Memory.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: The closest conceptual precursor, and the card does not cite it. Its 'memory hierarchy' says the write-plus-read cost of knowledge cannot reach zero, so placement should follow usage frequency: frequent knowledge goes to the weights, mid-frequency to explicit memory, rare knowledge to text RAG. This is the static, zero-hazard, offline version of the card's rent-or-buy rule. Cite it as the h->0 limit and add it as a named baseline.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Pretraining with hierarchical memories: separating long-tail and common knowledge.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: A static split decided at pretraining time: long-tail facts go to a large fetched memory bank, common knowledge to a small anchor model (160M anchor plus 18M fetched memory matches a model more than 2x larger). It shares the question of which knowledge belongs in the weights, but has no online decisions, no fact change and no drift price. It supports the 'reversible purchase' refinement: buying into a side memory instead of the base weights.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Pre-training Limited Memory Language Models with Internal and External Knowledge.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: LMLM (ICLR 2026) externalizes factual values to a database during pretraining, so revising or unlearning a fact means editing the store. It is the principled 'never buy' position, and it raises the prior that the card's honest answer at 0.5-1.5B is 'never buy volatile relations'. The card must position against it. The follow-up 'Auditing Forgetting in Limited Memory Language Models' (2607.00605, from search, not in the survey list) reports near-zero parametric leakage after store deletion, which supports treating store-side expiry as nearly free.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: WISE: Rethinking the Knowledge Memory for Lifelong Model Editing of Large Language Models.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: A parametric side memory with a router, separate from the main weights. It is a buy target whose purchase does not drift the base model and can be discarded at expiry. Add it as a second writer (via EasyEdit) for the 'reversible purchase' arm.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: ELDER: Enhancing Lifelong Model Editing with Mixture-of-LoRA.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Lifelong editing with LoRA experts. It is an alternative design for reversible purchases kept as deletable adapters. Relevant only to positioning; optional as a baseline.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: AlphaEdit: Null-Space Constrained Knowledge Editing for Language Models.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Already a planned writer. Under the card it is the irreversible-purchase case: when an AlphaEdit fact expires, the superseded key stays in the protected null space. Card #1 studies exactly this, so card #1's measured 'garbage' cost becomes the salvage penalty of an expired irreversible purchase.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Neighboring Perturbations of Knowledge Editing on Large Language Models.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Measures how edits damage neighbouring knowledge, which is half of the card's buy price D(f). Use its findings and probes to define and justify the neighbour-damage term, and cite it beside RL's Razor KL.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Online Adaptation of Language Models with a Memory of Amortized Contexts.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: MAC adapts online to a stream of documents (StreamingQA-style) by storing amortized context modulations. It is a cheap, deletable buy mechanism that sits between RAG and weight edits. Cite it as a related writer; it is too costly to train as a baseline under this budget.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Self-Updatable Large Language Models by Integrating Context into Model Parameters.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: An alternative internalization route (context into parameters by distillation). Cite it as a related writer; it is not needed as a baseline.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Zep: A Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: The store side of expiry: temporal validity intervals invalidate superseded facts at almost no cost. The RAG-only baseline must use a time-aware store like this, or 'rent' is strawmanned against 'buy'.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: From RAG to Memory: Non-Parametric Continual Learning for Large Language Models.
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Argues continual factual learning can stay non-parametric. It is positioning support for the 'rent' side. Its LLM-built index costs too much to use as the rent baseline here.

mapped.reframed_title: Rent, Buy, or Let It Expire: A Hazard-Adjusted Memory Hierarchy for Moving Changing Facts from a Store into a Small LM
mapped.reframed_one_liner: Memory^3's memory hierarchy puts frequently used knowledge in the weights, but facts change. This project derives an index for when to move a changing fact from a retrieval store into the weights: demand x retrieval rent x write generalization / (change hazard x drift price). It separates reversible purchases (side memory or a deletable LoRA) from irreversible ones (MEMIT/AlphaEdit into the base weights). Using trace-driven simulation on a real Wikidata change stream, it tests whether frequency-only placement misplaces volatile, frequently queried facts in 0.5-1.5B LMs.
changes: Repositioning: cite Memory^3's memory hierarchy as the static, zero-hazard special case and state the headline as a falsifiable claim. Frequency-only placement is suboptimal for changing facts. On the stream, frequency-ranked buying (the Memory^3 rule) should incur at least 20% more total cost and at least 30% more stale answers than the hazard-adjusted index. Put this claim in the abstract instead of 'an elegant rent-or-buy framing'.

Add the value side of a purchase: buying reduces rent only by the share of paraphrased queries the written fact answers without retrieval (g(f)). Forecast g(f) alongside the drift price B_hat(f), from the same pre-write signals plus a 20-step LoRA dry run on 3 paraphrases. At 0.5B, g is probably the binding constraint (Ovadia et al.; LMLM's motivation), so a model that prices drift but assumes perfect generalization overstates what buying is worth.

Split purchases into two types. Reversible: a WISE side memory or a per-month LoRA adapter, deleted at expiry, so the salvage cost is about zero. Irreversible: MEMIT/AlphaEdit into the base weights, whose salvage cost at expiry is measured as the extra drift and conflict rate of the counter-edit, reusing card #1's null-space measurements. The theory then becomes ski rental with resale. Report the competitive ratio for each purchase type, and the regime where an irreversible buy is never worth it.

Make evaluation trace-driven to cut GPU cost. Measure per-fact cost tables once on a 2k-fact panel: realized drift, neighbour damage, g(f), conflict penalty for a stale copy, and e(N) at 4 store sizes. Simulate all ~10 policies on CPU from these tables. Then run only the best 2-3 policies plus RAG-only live for 6-12 months of the stream, to check that the simulator's cost accounting holds under sequential-edit interference. A live/sim cost gap above 25% is itself a reported finding about non-additive interference (2607.11020).

Cut scope. Drop the Pythia checkpoint difference-in-differences (25 GPU-h; move it to future work). Drop 1.5B stream runs and keep 1.5B only in the forecasting study. Use one editor (AlphaEdit through EasyEdit, with GPT2-XL's official config as fallback) plus one reversible writer (LoRA r=8, or WISE). Target about 75 GPU-h for the paper instead of 160: covariance stats ~6, forecasting ~25, live validation ~25, retrieval curves and reruns ~20.

Reduce data engineering. First check whether WikiBigEdit's released snapshot-diff timesteps (and TemporalWiki's monthly diffsets) are numerous and frequent enough to serve as the change stream. If so, use them, and crawl Wikidata revision history only for a sample of about 1k (s, r) pairs to fit per-relation Weibull hazards. Pageviews stay as a cheap API crawl. The number and spacing of WikiBigEdit timesteps are unverified here; check them in week 1.

Add a go/no-go test for the store-size externality in week 1. Measure recall@k for bge-small and BM25 at N = 1k vs 50k with same-relation distractors. If e(N) rises by less than about 5 points, drop the externality term and say so. The paper then becomes per-fact ski rental with expiry and resale, a narrower but cleaner claim.

Make the RAG-only baseline time-aware, with Zep-style validity intervals and latest-value-wins on retrieval. Store-side expiry should be nearly free, so 'buy' is compared against the strongest cheap 'rent'.

Write the policy in the survey's operator vocabulary. It schedules F (parametric internalization), E (updating at expiry; forgetting as store eviction and demotion) and R timing (skip retrieval for bought facts). Present the empirical buy/hold/demote trajectories as evidence for the survey's claim that long-term vs short-term status emerges from temporal patterns of F/E/R, here driven by demand and hazard.

Add a CPU-only learned comparator in the simulator: a contextual bandit or tabular RL policy trained on simulated streams. This speaks to frontier 7.3 (RL decides when to consolidate) without GPU RL. The claim is that the analytic index matches it at a fraction of the sample cost and comes with a worst-case bound.

Keep the ALLOT kill condition and resolve it before any GPU spend: read ALLOT's method section for demand, expiry or online components. Add LMLM to the kill logic. If the week-1 panel shows median g(f) < 0.3 for both writers at 0.5B and 1.5B, publish a short 'never buy at small scale' regime-map note (theory plus measured tables) instead of the full stream paper.

LMLM stance, 'never buy': a time-aware RAG-only store with Zep-style validity intervals
WISE side memory as a reversible writer (EasyEdit), compared with AlphaEdit/MEMIT into the base weights at a matched write budget

mapped.rationale:
The survey weakens the card's positioning more than its 'still new' list admits. The rent-or-buy core already exists in a survey-listed work the card never cites. Memory^3's 'memory hierarchy' allocates knowledge to weights, explicit memory or RAG by usage frequency to minimize write-plus-read cost (confirmed by search: arxiv.org/abs/2407.01178). Two other survey-listed works make the same store/weights split statically at pretraining time: 'Pretraining with hierarchical memories' (arxiv.org/abs/2510.02375) and LMLM (arxiv.org/abs/2505.15962). LMLM in particular argues that facts belong outside the weights because they change. That raises the prior on the plan's own risk that buying never pays at 0.5-1.5B, which would collapse every policy toward RAG-only and leave the competitive-ratio headline with nothing to measure. The plan also prices only the cost of a purchase (KL drift), not its value (whether the write generalizes to paraphrases). It spends 160 GPU-h, flagged as optimistic, plus a heavy Wikidata crawl before the main result appears, and the ALLOT scoop check is still open.

What survives is real and well aimed. The online, change-aware move between the dense factual x token-level cell (84 works) and the sparser factual x parametric cell (16 works) has no listed method. Expiry, synchronizing a stale parametric copy with the store, and reversible vs irreversible purchases address a blind spot a third-party critique attributes to the survey. Reframed as a hazard-adjusted generalization of Memory^3's hierarchy, with a falsifiable claim that frequency-only placement fails for volatile, frequently queried facts, the idea is sharper and better positioned. With trace-driven simulation it costs about 75 GPU-h. Within Arc 2 it sits best as the economics and theory piece that connects card #3 (selling the store copy) and card #1 (the salvage cost of an expired irreversible edit). It stays a standalone project rather than a merge because its theory and simulator are separate deliverables, but it should not lead Arc 2. Promote it back to Tier B only if the week-1 panel shows median paraphrase generalization g >= 0.5 for at least one writer and a non-trivial e(N) slope, and the ALLOT check comes back clean. Sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2407.01178v1, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.02375, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2505.15962, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.00605

mapped.survey_function: factual (user-centric and environment facts that change over time)
dynamics_ops: evolution:updating (conflict resolution, the primary operator: the overwrite decision itself)
evolution:forgetting (temporary sub-states expire; low-mass run-length hypotheses are pruned)

mapped.cell_density: dense: Factual x Token-level has 84 listed works, the densest cell in the survey list. About 10 of them touch the updating or forgetting operator for changing facts: Mem0, Memory-R1, Zep, A-MEM, RGMem, Hindsight, Timeline-based memory, MemoryBank, Mem-alpha and Generative agents. No title among the 84 mentions Bayesian, change-point, uncertainty or calibrated updating (checked by grep), so the framing is distinct, but the operator is not empty.
frontier_links: 7.2 Automated memory management. Between the survey's two routes, handcrafted heuristics and learned policies, #10 offers a third: a derived, calibrated policy whose two parameters per attribute class (hazard and stance noise) are fit by empirical Bayes and can be inspected.

7.3 RL meets agent memory. Memory-R1 learns the UPDATE vs NOOP choice by RL, and Mem-alpha learns memory construction by RL. #10 can test whether a closed-form gate matches a learned gate when both get the same calibration data.

Trustworthy memory. The slots give calibrated posteriors, an evidence trail for explainability, and a closed-form flip cost: the number of low-reliability assertions needed to overwrite a slot (1 for latest-wins). This addresses robustness to hearsay, hallucinated extractions and injected assertions.

7.8 Human-cognitive connections. Entrenchment under Benna-Fusi/Memini coupled fast/slow edges and under MemoryBank's Ebbinghaus strength rule is the external-store analogue of proactive interference (cf. 2603.00270, PI-LLM).

The Section 3 position that short- vs long-term memory emerge from the temporal patterns of F/E/R rather than from separate modules. Temporary-scope sub-states with expiry and hazard give short-term and permanent behaviour from one slot mechanism.
mapped.survey_claim_tested: Frontier 7.3/7.2 holds that decisions such as when to update or consolidate should move from handcrafted rules to learned, policy-driven (RL) memory managers (Memory-R1, Mem-alpha). #10 tests a third option on the updating operator. Hold extraction fixed and give both gates the same calibration split. If a two-parameter-per-class Bayes quickest-change gate ties or beats a learned UPDATE/NOOP gate at <=1k calibration examples, the case for RL on factual updating shrinks to extraction, not gating. If the learned gate wins clearly, the survey's position is confirmed. A secondary, sharper target is a survey-listed paper's claim. RGMem reports a critical evolution threshold (theta=3) that it says is the same on LoCoMo and PersonaMem, and reads this as a property of multi-scale memory. The closed form predicts that this threshold moves with hazard and noise.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: RGMem: Renormalization Group-based Memory Evolution for Language Agent User Profile
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Closest listed work. It separates fast-changing evidence from slow traits and updates the profile only when accumulated evidence passes a threshold theta_inf. It reports a subcritical regime, where noise triggers updates, and a supercritical regime, where the profile is rigid, with a sharp optimum at theta=3 on both LoCoMo and PersonaMem, which it calls dataset-invariant. This is already the card's latency vs false-update trade-off, implemented as a tuned count threshold: the strongest k-confirm-style baseline. Code: github.com/fenhg297/RGMem. Source: search snippets (https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.16392); the full method was not read.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Memory-R1: Enhancing Large Language Model Agents to Manage and Utilize Memories via Reinforcement Learning
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Its RL-trained memory manager chooses ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP, so the overwrite decision is learned end to end. This is the frontier-7.3 competitor that the plan omits.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Zep: A Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Bi-temporal edges are invalidated on contradiction, not deleted. This already covers the card's 'superseded values kept as version siblings' and the previous/first-value queries. Already a baseline (Graphiti). The remaining delta is expiry with revert to the parent value, which needs checking in the Graphiti code.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Towards Lifelong Dialogue Agents via Timeline-based Memory Management
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Keeps outdated memories linked on timelines instead of deleting them. Together with Zep, this means version history is not a contribution.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Hindsight is 20/20: Building Agent Memory that Retains, Recalls, and Reflects
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Separates facts from beliefs. Its opinion network stores beliefs with confidence scores that are reported to update as new evidence arrives; the update rule was not found in snippets. It is MIT open source and reports very strong LongMemEval accuracy (83.6% with a 20B open model; 91.4% with Gemini-3 Pro, partly vendor-reported), so a LongMemEval-KU headline win is unrealistic. Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.12818

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Mem0: Building production-ready ai agents with scalable long-term memory
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: A prompted LLM manager with ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP: an implicit, unaccountable overwrite decision. Already a baseline.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Memory evolution rewrites linked notes when new notes arrive, so it is an implicit updating operator. Already a baseline.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Memorybank: Enhancing large language models with long-term memory
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: An Ebbinghaus forgetting curve whose strength is reinforced on recall. This is a repetition-weighted consolidation rule in the factual-token cell that the entrenchment law should cover alongside Memini.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Mem-α: Learning Memory Construction via Reinforcement Learning

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Generative agents: Interactive simulacra of human behavior
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Recency x importance x relevance retrieval scoring is a retrieval-side analogue of fixed-gain recency weighting, and the importance weighting may also entrench.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: From RAG to Memory: Non-Parametric Continual Learning for Large Language Models
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: HippoRAG 2. Already a baseline, as a non-parametric store with no explicit overwrite.

mapped.reframed_title: Overwrite or Wait? A Closed-Form Overwrite Threshold That Explains Threshold-Gated, RL-Gated and Multi-Timescale Agent Memory
mapped.reframed_one_liner: The plan derives the Bayes-optimal overwrite rule for factual slot memory, k*(h, eps) ~ ceil(log((1-h)/h) / log((1-eps)/eps)), and shows that latest-wins (eps=0), k-confirm and RGMem's threshold (constant h and eps), fixed-gain EMA and Memini fast/slow edges are special cases or approximations of it. It tests two predictions: the optimal threshold moves with hazard and noise, contrary to RGMem's invariant theta=3, and repetition-weighted rules entrench linearly in R. It then shows that a stance- and class-adaptive gate beats any single global threshold by an amount that grows with the spread of k* across the stream, and matches a learned UPDATE/NOOP gate when calibration data are small.
changes: Lead with theory and its predictions, not the method. State k*(h, eps) and the entrenchment slope as the main results. Present latest-wins (eps=0), the k-confirm and RGMem count thresholds (h and eps constant), fixed-gain EMA and Memini edges as special cases or approximations. Example values: h=0.05, eps=0.2 gives k*=3; h=0.01, eps=0.3 gives 6; h=0.1, eps=0.1 gives 2; eps=0 gives 1 (latest-wins).

Admit the weak point up front. When h and eps are constant, the Bayes gate is the same as a tuned count threshold, so its expected gain over the best global threshold on homogeneous streams is about 0. Make the main method plot the gain over the best global threshold against the spread of k* across the stance x attribute-class mix. Replace the kill criterion 'beat tuned k-confirm by >=5 points' with two conditions that must both hold: a gain of at least 5 points on mixed-reliability streams, and a gain of no more than 1 point on homogeneous streams, as predicted.

Add an RGMem threshold test in weeks 1-2, on CPU plus about $50-100 of API calls. Read github.com/fenhg297/RGMem to confirm what theta_inf counts. Run its update rule on ReBind-lite streams with h in {0.01, 0.05, 0.2} and eps in {0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.4}, and sweep theta in {1..8}. The prediction is that the best theta tracks k*(h, eps) with Spearman >= 0.8. If the peak moves by 2 or more across the grid, RGMem's dataset-invariance claim is falsified. Add PersonaMem, which RGMem evaluates on, so the comparison also runs on RGMem's own benchmark.

Add a learned-vs-derived gate test for frontier 7.3, about 10-15 GPU-h. Train a LoRA UPDATE/NOOP classifier on Qwen2.5-1.5B (SFT, with GRPO optional) on the same calibration split that the empirical-Bayes fit uses. Plot decision accuracy and false-update rate against calibration size, 50 to 5k examples. The prediction is that the Bayes gate ties or wins below about 1k examples. Use Memory-R1 only as an end-to-end reference on the MemOps recency_trap, and only if a checkpoint is released; do not retrain 7-8B RL.

Add 'decide at read time' baselines: the event-statement store from 'A Simple Yet Strong Baseline...' and a full-context reader whose evidence is tagged with stance. Compare them at matched reader-context token budgets and over the number of updates N. The claim is narrower than before: the slot posterior is a compact sufficient statistic that wins when the budget is small or N is large, where in-context proactive interference bites (2603.00270, PI-LLM). Report the crossover budget.

Stop claiming version siblings and history queries as contributions, since Zep's bi-temporal invalidation and Timeline-based memory already do this; keep them as infrastructure. Keep temporary scope, but test it directly against Zep. Measure expiry-recovery accuracy when a temporary fact ends: the gate restores the parent value, while Zep presumably leaves the old edge invalidated. Verify that in the Graphiti code before claiming it.

Generalize the entrenchment law beyond Memini. Derive and simulate on CPU the update latency L(R, lag) for three survey-relevant rules: Memini or Benna-Fusi edges, MemoryBank's recall-reinforced Ebbinghaus strength, and RGMem's accumulated-evidence threshold. Predict which entrench linearly in R and which are bounded. This makes the law a statement about the Evolution:consolidation operator, not about one system.

Add a closed-form flip-cost metric for the trustworthy-memory frontier: the number of contradicting assertions at a given stance needed to overwrite a slot. It is 1 for latest-wins and log((1-h)/h)/log((1-eps_s)/eps_s) for the gate. Validate it by injecting false hearsay or asserted values into MemOps-style streams. Report it next to update latency as the two axes of one Pareto front.

Cut compute from about 120 GPU-h to about 30-40 GPU-h plus about $300-500 of API calls. Use API extraction (gpt-4o-mini) with the oracle-extraction arm as the headline result. Drop the Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen3-8B serving and the local 128K arm (use an API long-context reader on a subset). Drop the leave-one-system-out predictive-validity analysis, which has only about 10 systems. Make the per-session LoRA entrenchment arm optional, or fold it into #1 or #9, where parametric revision chains already exist.

Lower the LongMemEval-KU and FactConsolidation goal to a no-harm check: within 2 points of latest-wins with the same reader. Hindsight-level systems already score very high on LongMemEval, so it cannot be a headline result. Put the headline on MemOps recency_trap, the BBT staleness benchmark, LoCoMo-mined natural corrections and the k*-spread grid.

Position the work with the survey's vocabulary: a calibrated Evolution:Updating operator for factual token-level memory. Say explicitly that none of the 84 Factual x Token-level titles in the survey list mentions Bayesian, change-point or calibrated updating. Share the per-attribute-class hazard estimator with #9, as its change forecast, and the entrenchment theory with #5 (Arc 3).

mapped.rationale: Read critically, the survey makes the card's method-first claim weaker than stated. #10 sits in the densest cell of the survey list (Factual x Token-level, 84 works), and its target operator, Evolution:Updating, is already handled by several listed systems. RGMem already reports the card's noise vs rigidity trade-off with an accumulated-evidence threshold tuned to theta=3. Zep and Timeline-based memory already keep superseded versions. Hindsight already keeps confidence-scored beliefs that update with evidence. Memory-R1 learns UPDATE/NOOP by RL. Worse for the current plan, when hazard and noise are constant the Bayes gate reduces to a count threshold, so the GO and kill test 'beat a tuned k-confirm by >=5 points' will probably fail on homogeneous data. What survives, and becomes sharper, is the theory. A closed-form k*(h, eps) unifies latest-wins, k-confirm, RGMem, EMA and Memini as special cases or approximations. It makes falsifiable predictions against a survey-listed paper (RGMem's invariant critical threshold should move with h and eps) and a survey frontier (an RL-learned overwrite policy vs a derived one at matched calibration data). It also predicts exactly when the adaptive gate should win: in proportion to the spread of k* across stances and attribute classes. Reframed this way, the paper is cheaper (about 30-40 GPU-h plus API, mostly CPU theory), honest about where the method cannot win, and engaged with the survey's 7.2, 7.3 and trustworthy-memory frontiers. Keep it at Tier B, theory-first. Do not merge: it shares the Arc 3 entrenchment theory with #5 and the hazard estimator with #9, but its object is different (overwrite decisions in an external factual store). Caveat: the RGMem and Hindsight details come from search snippets (https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.16392, https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.12818, https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.17208). Before building on them, read what RGMem's theta_inf counts and Hindsight's confidence update rule.

evolution:consolidation (session-boundary fold of latent working memory into persistent memory)
evolution:updating (recency-weighted RLS resolves contradicting sessions)
evolution:forgetting (forgetting factor rho, plus the model's own gate decay acting on an injected initial state)

mapped.cell_density: Source cell working-latent is dense (22 listed), but nearly all of it is KV-cache compression (H2O, SnapKV, Scissorhands, RazorAttention) or trained memory architectures (Titans, LM2, Memorizing Transformers). No listed work consolidates a recurrent state across sessions. Target cells: factual-latent is sparse (8: M+, Memory^3, R3Mem, Memoria, ...), all of them trained architectures. Factual-parametric is moderate (16), mostly editing plus two context-to-parameter works (MAC, SELF-PARAM). Working-parametric is sparse (2), and one of the two is a linear-attention LM (Lightning Attention). The survey files Lightning Attention under parametric and Titans under latent, so its own grid is inconsistent about where a linear-attention fast state belongs. That boundary is exactly this card's object. The 'empty transition' is real inside the survey, but the second-round search already found close work outside it (PRECOG/SMC, State Soup, Sleep, FAAST), so sparsity here does not mean novelty.
frontier_links: 7.2 Automated memory management: replace heuristic merge rules (State Soup averaging, PRECOG softmax top-k, MAC's nearest-neighbour modulation averaging) with an objective-derived ridge merge. This is a third option between hand-set heuristics and the learned/RL policies the survey favours, and it fits when the memory is linear.

7.8 Human-cognitive connections: the fold is an explicit Atkinson-Shiffrin short-term -> long-term transfer, a 'sleep' phase like the gradient-based Sleep paper but closed-form. Variant (a) vs (b) asks whether long-term memory needs its own store.
Section 3 / dynamics position that short-term vs long-term memory emerge from F/E/R timing rather than from separate modules [SNIP-level evidence]: directly testable here (see survey_claim_tested).
7.1 Retrieval -> generation (weak link): a folded state is a retrieval-free memory, in contrast to MAC/PRECOG retrieve-then-aggregate. Use only as framing, not as a claim.

Trustworthy memory (explainability): the per-head map (decay half-life, state rank, query/key alignment) makes an opaque latent memory auditable. The privacy claim should be dropped unless an inversion test is added.

mapped.survey_claim_tested: Survey position [SNIP]: short-term vs long-term memory 'emerge from the temporal patterns with which formation, evolution and retrieval are engaged', not from separate architectural modules. Test: fold the same sessions into (a) the model's own recurrent initial state (same module, LTM differs from STM only by when E runs) vs (b) a separate non-decaying read term (separate module). Prediction: (a) ≈ (b) in no-decay DeltaNet heads, which supports the claim. In decaying heads (RWKV-7, GLA), (a) collapses relative to (b) once the decay half-life is shorter than the question length, which would show the claim fails for gated recurrent memory: long-term memory then needs its own non-decaying store. A secondary [SEC]-level claim, 'parametric memory is efficient but suffers catastrophic forgetting', is probed by whether reference-Gram protection keeps the latent->parametric move at generic KL <= 0.02 and a zero-shot lm-eval drop of <= 0.5 points.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Online Adaptation of Language Models with a Memory of Amortized Contexts
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Same pipeline: each document becomes a compact parameter-space memory unit, and many units are merged into one modulation for a frozen LM. MAC (arXiv 2403.04317) meta-trains an amortization encoder and a question-conditioned aggregation network (GPT2-Large, LLaMA-2 7B; StreamingQA, SQuAD, ArchivalQA). Its memory-bank shrinking merges nearest-neighbour modulations by cosine averaging, a heuristic in-place merge. The fold replaces the trained encoder with the model's own end state and the learned aggregator with a question-independent ridge solve. MAC itself is too costly to retrain, but its NN-averaging rule is a cheap baseline and its protocol is the community standard.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Self-Updatable Large Language Models by Integrating Context into Model Parameters
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Same goal and evaluation: integrate sequential contexts into parameters, then answer without context, scored by efficacy (recent) and retention (old) over sequential injection (50 sequences, QA-F1). SELF-PARAM (arXiv 2410.00487, ICLR 2025) uses KL context distillation on self-generated QA, with MLP training on OpenLLaMA-3B and LoRA on 7-8B models. It is the right gradient competitor and should replace 'LoRA SFT on session text'.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: M+: Extending MemoryLLM with Scalable Long-Term Memory
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: A persistent latent repository in hidden-state space that the same model reads. It requires a trained ~8B model. It is the trained counterpart of variant (a), so it serves as a positioning reference, not a runnable baseline.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Separates test-time contextual long-term memory from a 'persistent memory' learned offline. The fold builds persistent memory post hoc from contextual memory, without training. This is the conceptual frame for variant (b) as a separate store.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: AlphaEdit: Null-Space Constrained Knowledge Editing for Language Models
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Source of the protection idea (here a soft ridge term lambda*C_ref, not an exact null space) and a CounterFact-track baseline. Already in the plan.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Various Lengths, Constant Speed: Efficient Language Modeling with Lightning Attention
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: A linear-attention LM that the survey files under Working/Parametric while Titans sits under Working/Latent. Cite it to motivate that the latent/parametric status of a fast state is ambiguous, and that (a) vs (b) makes the distinction operational.

survey_listed_overlaps.title: Adapting Language Models to Compress Contexts
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: AutoCompressor, together with 'Learning to Compress Prompts with Gist Tokens' and 'In-Context Autoencoder for Context Compression in a Large Language Model', trains a per-context latent compressor whose outputs are reused later. Those methods compose by concatenation, so memory grows with N. A recurrent end state is a free, untrained compressor that must be composed in place at fixed size, which is the gap the ridge fold fills. These are related work, not baselines (trained, transformer-only).

survey_listed_overlaps.title: WISE: Rethinking the Knowledge Memory for Lifelong Model Editing of Large Language Models
survey_listed_overlaps.overlap: Lifelong sequential editing with a side memory and routing, which handles repeated or contradicting edits. Relevant on the CounterFact contradiction track as related work. Porting it to SSMs is not worth the budget.

mapped.reframed_title: Does Long-Term Memory Need Its Own Store? Training-Free Folding of Session States in Frozen Recurrent LMs
mapped.reframed_one_liner: Consolidate many sessions' end states of a frozen linear-attention/SSM LM with a recency-weighted, generic-protected ridge fold. Deposit the result either in the model's own recurrent state (same module) or in a separate non-decaying read term, then map per head, by decay half-life, state rank and query/key alignment, when the same-module route suffices. Compare against brute-force bank-and-route, State Soup/PRECOG/MAC-style heuristic merges and SELF-PARAM-style context distillation, on the survey's efficacy/retention protocol.
changes: Make variant (a) vs (b) the headline experiment instead of an ablation, framed as a test of the survey's 'STM/LTM emerge from F/E/R timing, not separate modules' position. Pre-register: per-head (b)-(a) recall gap rises with decay rate (Spearman >= 0.5 across heads, pooled over RWKV-7, DeltaNet and GLA). This diagnostic result survives even if the method claim dies.

Delete the storage claim. With O(1) running sums (numerator and denominator per head), the fold stores roughly 25-50 MB fp32 for a 1.3-1.5B model (fewer if only 10-30% of heads are folded), against about 1-2 KB of text per 300-token session. Text is cheaper until thousands to tens of thousands of sessions, far beyond N <= 100. Drop the privacy claim too, unless a state/Gram inversion test is added. Restate the advantages as zero context tokens at inference, seconds-long consolidation with no gradients, and a bounded generic-KL shift.

Fix an internal contradiction. Bottom-up fresh-query refitting (method step 3) needs inputs re-run after lower layers are folded, so it cannot coexist with 'no text is kept'. Split the method into two named regimes and report both at matched storage: Streaming (O(1) running sums, no refit, no text) and Sleep-phase (session text buffered until the fold, refit allowed, then discarded).

Replace 'LoRA SFT on session text' with SELF-PARAM-style KL context distillation into LoRA as the main gradient competitor (same 1.3-1.5B models; about 15 GPU-h). Keep gradient state tuning (S0/RWKV state tuning) as the second gradient competitor.

Add the brute-force baseline the survey's complexity-bias critique calls for: a state bank with BM25- or oracle-routed top-1 state injection. It is exact per PRECOG's top-1 case and is the latent upper bound, with storage linear in N. Share the bank code and framing with #2 ('bank vs fold').

Add MAC's nearest-neighbour pairwise averaging (cosine) of stored states down to a fixed bank size K as a third heuristic merge, next to State Soup averaging and PRECOG softmax top-k. The ridge fold must beat all three as N grows.

Adopt the survey-listed factual-parametric protocol vocabulary and metrics: efficacy (last 1-2 sessions) and retention (sessions older than 5) under sequential injection, scored by QA-F1 and exact match. Add one real-text track with short answers from SQuAD or StreamingQA (as in MAC), filtered to questions the base model answers correctly in context. Drop TOFU to save cost.

Cut models to cut cost: RWKV-7 1.5B (decaying generalized delta) and DeltaNet 1.3B (no decay) as the main pair, with GLA 1.3B as the third point of the decay map. Drop Mamba2, where the re-solve variant is out of distribution and channel-wise discretisation makes it a special case. Revised budget is about 75-90 GPU-h, not 120.

Add a CPU-only Day-1 toy. In a single linear-attention or delta-rule layer the fold is exact, so derive closed-form recall vs N for ridge, average, softmax-composition and NN-averaging merges, with and without contradictions and decay. Reuse #5's delta-rule algebra and simulation code. This gives the diagnostic map its theoretical skeleton at zero GPU cost.

Revise the go/no-go to two independent gates. Method GO keeps the existing criteria and adds 'fold within 10 points of bank+top-1 routing at N=10 while using no routing'. Diagnostic GO is the (b)-(a) vs decay Spearman >= 0.5. If only the diagnostic gate passes, write a short analysis paper or workshop paper.

If #5's nonlinear test passes, import the ridge fold into #5's testbed as an explicit session-boundary consolidation operator (W_slow <- fold at reset) to compare with #5's derived downscaling schedule (<= 5 GPU-h).

Optional stretch, only if #2's oracle test passes (<= 10 GPU-h): compare bank+route against confidence-weighted averaging of banked TTT3R states for a revisited scene. This carries the 'bank vs fold' question into the user's 3D arc, which the survey does not cover.

mapped.rationale: The survey does not take the card's remaining novelty (the protected recency ridge fold, bottom-up refit and the per-head map). It does show the idea is weaker than the card presents in three ways. (1) The goal itself, integrating sequential contexts into parameters for continual factual recall, is an established line inside the survey's own factual-parametric cell. MAC and SELF-PARAM both do it, with standard protocols (efficacy/retention; StreamingQA, SQuAD, ArchivalQA) that the card ignores. MAC even has a heuristic in-place merge of stored memory units. (2) Two card claims do not survive a check. Stored bytes favour text, not statistics, at the planned N <= 100. And bottom-up refitting needs replayed inputs, which contradicts 'no text is kept'. (3) On raw recall the method will probably lose to brute-force bank+top-1 routing and to SELF-PARAM-style distillation. Its edge is only zero context cost and gradient-free consolidation, and that matters little to the survey's agent-memory audience, which works with API transformers. What the survey adds is a sharper, cheap and falsifiable scientific question. The card moves latent working memory into factual memory, and its two deployment variants map exactly onto 'same module' vs 'separate store'. That lets it test the survey's claim that STM/LTM emerge from dynamics timing rather than architecture, and the per-head decay map should settle it for gated recurrent LMs. Recommendation: demote from lead-candidate Tier B to a diagnostic-first Arc-3 chapter at about 75-90 GPU-h, co-scheduled with #5. The method claim stays conditional on beating bank+route and the three heuristic merges. Evidence quality: the STM/LTM position comes from search snippets of the survey, not the PDF, so quote it carefully. MAC and SELF-PARAM details come from search results ([SELF-PARAM arXiv 2410.00487](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.00487v2); [MAC arXiv 2403.04317](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.04317v2)). Model state sizes are approximate (configs from memory).

mapped.reframed_one_liner: Use GT-overlap revisit strata and a future-attention reference to test Scissorhands' persistence-of-importance hypothesis on StreamVGGT/STream3R. Then decompose the headroom: how much a pose-only FOV oracle recovers (geometry) and how much a small set of RazorAttention-style 'revisit heads' recovers (heads).

newIdeas.title: Ghosts in the pointer memory: does stale learned 3D memory corrupt what the model sees now, and does free-space contradiction fix it where attention-based eviction cannot?
newIdeas.one_liner: In explicit learned 3D memories (Point3R pointers, StreamVGGT KV tokens), entries left behind by objects that were moved or removed are not just map debris, because every new frame reads them. This card first tests whether those stale entries hurt present depth and pose (an oracle-deletion test on 3RScan rescans). It then compares a training-free free-space-contradiction deletion rule with the attention-frequency and importance criteria that published 3D KV-eviction methods use.

newIdeas.differentiation:
The operator itself is not new. Removing stale geometry with free-space evidence goes back to Keller 2013 and ReFusion 2019, then POCD, GaME 2025, and Changes-in-Real-Time 2025/26. Argos-SLAM (2610.10181, if it checks out) already pairs a feed-forward VGGT-family backbone with cross-visit change-aware mapping. Pitching this as "contradiction-driven forgetting for 3D maps" would be scooped.

Three things are still defensible:
(1) The interference question. In Point3R and StreamVGGT, memory is not an output map but an input that every later frame cross-attends to. Nobody has measured whether entries made stale by world change degrade present depth and pose, or tested this with GT-oracle deletion on changed versus static pixels. RayMap3R and TTSA3R/MeMix gate writes. GaME, Argos and Changes-in-Real-Time clean the output map. GHOST names dynamic scenes as open for KV eviction.
(2) A mechanistic reason ghosts persist in pointer memory. Point3R fuses by Euclidean proximity, and Ray-Aware likely replaces only near new observations. A removed object therefore leaves pointers that nothing new lands near, so they are never merged or replaced.
(3) An evaluation of the published 3D KV-eviction criteria under world change: InfiniteVGGT's query-key similarity, Evict3R's attention statistics, STAC's spatiotemporal persistence, GHOST's geometry score, and Point3R/Ray-Aware fusion. This directly tests the survey's persistence-of-importance assumption (Scissorhands). The survey list has no streaming 3D model, so placing this in the cell (Evolution: updating/forgetting for factual latent memory) is new framing.

Everything defensible depends on H1. If oracle deletion does not help present perception, this collapses into map hygiene that Argos/GaME already cover.
newIdeas.revised_kill_criterion:
- Kill as a methods paper if GT-oracle quarantine improves changed or vacated-ray AbsRel by less than 5% relative and B pose by less than 5% over carry, or if random-quarantine matches it. Stale entries would then not interfere with present perception; the remaining problem is output-map hygiene, which Argos-SLAM, GaME and classical free-space carving already cover. In that case, put the negative result (with the attention-mass diagnostic) into #13 as a 3RScan plasticity finding.
- Kill the operator, but keep the diagnostic, if contradiction quarantine recovers less than 25% of the oracle gain because of pose noise, even with uncertainty-scaled margins.
- Downgrade H2 to a footnote if the best of frequency, similarity and importance eviction recovers at least as much as contradiction does at equal memory size.

original.title: Ghosts in the pointer memory: contradiction-driven forgetting for learned 3D memory after the world changes
original.one_liner: When a revisited room has changed, stale entries in an explicit learned spatial memory (Point3R pointers, StreamVGGT KV tokens) are not inert map debris, because every new frame reads them. Delete or quarantine an entry when the current view shows free space where it sits, and test this against the time, frequency and importance criteria that agent memories normally use.
original.survey_cell: Factual x Latent (8 papers in the survey list), here as explicit 3D-addressed latent entries. Lifecycle operator: Evolution E, specifically Updating (conflict resolution) and Forgetting.
original.survey_hook: The survey splits Evolution into consolidation, updating and forgetting, and files conflict resolution in external stores under updating. Its multimodal-memory frontier targets embodied agents, but its paper list contains no streaming 3D model. Its spatial and embodied entries (Mem2Ego, Embodied VideoAgent, MemoryVLA's merging of adjacent similar entries) handle redundancy, not contradiction. Scissorhands' 'persistence of importance' hypothesis (survey working-latent cell) predicts the failure tested here: a stale entry keeps its importance, because new frames that conflict with it still attend to it. The digest could not confirm the survey's exact forgetting sub-criteria, so time, frequency and importance are used as the field's standard criteria.
original.big_picture_hook: This is the external-store row ('retrieval interference and drift') plus the lesson that external memory moves the stability-plasticity dilemma to memory access (2604.27003): old and new entries compete when they are read. 2605.12978 shows useful memories turn harmful when continuously rewritten. This is the same failure, caused by the world changing rather than by the rewriter. Point3R's own limitations section says its growing set of pointer positions interferes with later pose estimation, which is direct evidence inside the doc's 3D section.
original.task:
Cross-session streaming reconstruction in a changed space: stream session A, then session B of the same room after objects were moved, added or removed, carrying the memory across.
- Data: about 40 3RScan reference/rescan pairs with at least 3 changed objects (Tango RGB-D, provided rescan-to-reference transforms, per-instance change annotations). B's start frame is chosen by GT co-visibility with A's end, so registration does not confound the result. Pairs with no annotated change serve as a control. Optional controlled set: object rearrangements rendered in ReplicaCAD/Habitat. A return test (A-B-A') brings moved objects back.
- Models: Point3R (github.com/YkiWu/Point3R, NeurIPS 2025, arXiv 2507.02863) as the main model. StreamVGGT as the second model; its cached tokens get 3D positions from their frame's predicted pointmap. CUT3R/TTT3R (cut3r_512_dpt_4_64.pth) as a latent-memory reference arm that is measured only.
- Metrics: depth AbsRel and delta<1.25 on B frames, split into changed-object pixels and static pixels (3RScan instance masks projected with GT poses); B pose ATE/RPE in A's frame; ghost rate (final-map points inside the old volumes of moved objects); Chamfer distance to B's mesh in changed regions; memory size.
original.mechanism:
Training-free, and run at keyframes only (the survey notes F/E/R need not run every step).
- Evidence: each memory entry p whose 3D position lies in the current frustum is projected with the predicted pose. If the predicted depth at that pixel is larger than p's depth by a margin, with high decoder confidence, p sits in observed free space and gains contradiction evidence. If p agrees with the observed surface, its evidence drops. If p is behind the surface, it is occluded and left alone. Evidence accumulates as OctoMap-style log-odds weighted by confidence.
- Action: past a threshold, p is either deleted or quarantined. A quarantined entry is masked from attention but kept, and is restored if later views support it again.
- StreamVGGT: the same test is applied to cached tokens, with attention masking.
- Baseline arms: no forgetting (default); time (age cap or FIFO); frequency (H2O-style attention-hit counts); importance (confidence); redundancy pruning (Ray-Aware Pointer Memory 2605.05749, if its code is released); MemoryVLA-style similarity merging; a global reset at the start of B (LongStream-style); and oracle deletion of entries inside GT changed volumes as the upper bound.
original.hypothesis:
- H1 (interference): carrying A's memory helps static pixels in B but hurts changed-object pixels. Oracle deletion improves changed-pixel AbsRel by at least 10% relative over carry and leaves static pixels unchanged (within 2%).
- H2 (the standard criteria are wrong): frequency-based eviction does no better than no forgetting on changed pixels, and possibly worse, because conflicting frames keep attending to stale entries. At equal memory size, contradiction-driven forgetting recovers at least 50% of the oracle gain, while the best of time, frequency and importance recovers at most 25%.
- H3: on A-B-A' return sequences, quarantine beats deletion by at least 5% on the returned objects.
- If H1 fails, the result is only classical map hygiene, which Keller et al. 2013 already solved.
original.first_experiment:
About 10 GPU-hours over 2 weeks.
- Week 1: hook Point3R's memory (pointer positions, features, attention weights) and project the 3RScan change masks into each frame.
- Week 2: on 20 3RScan pairs, run five conditions: reset at B, carry, carry plus oracle deletion, carry plus contradiction deletion, and carry plus frequency eviction. Report changed-pixel and static-pixel AbsRel on B and B's pose in A's frame.
- GO if both hold:
  - oracle deletion beats carry by at least 10% relative changed-pixel AbsRel, with static pixels within 2%;
  - contradiction deletion recovers at least 50% of that gain, with a paired-bootstrap CI over pairs that excludes 0.
original.kill_criterion:
- Kill if oracle deletion improves changed-pixel AbsRel or B pose by less than 5% over carry. Stale entries would then not interfere with present perception; only the map needs cleaning, and classical free-space carving already covers that.
- Kill if contradiction deletion recovers less than 25% of the oracle gain because of pose noise. A third-party review flags the directional check in Ray-Aware Pointer Memory as fragile to pose noise.
- If B fails to register on more than 30% of pairs, move the main set to ReplicaCAD renders before killing.

newIdeas.title: Predict before you look: prequential conformal routing between generated and retrieved recall in a streaming 3D state
newIdeas.one_liner: Before each new frame arrives, a frozen CUT3R/TTT3R predicts that frame by querying its live state at the frame's pose (generation) and by reprojecting stored keyframes (retrieval). When the frame arrives, the prediction is scored against what the camera actually sees. These free labels, collected before and after looking, calibrate a conformal router that chooses generation, retrieval or abstention for each pixel, and an eviction rule that drops keyframes the state can already regenerate.

newIdeas.differentiation:
Status of each part of the original idea:
- **Scooped.** H2's headline, that CUT3R's confidence is overconfident, is already shown: 2608.29705 reports about 40% coverage at a nominal 90%. Conformal bounds for novel-view geometry already exist for 3DGS (VSCP 2609.10307). Generative read-out at virtual cameras is native to CUT3R and ZipMap, so it cannot be a contribution.
- **Methodological flaw in the original.** Its GT-free labels come from re-querying G at past keyframes and comparing with the stored predictions. That measures self-consistency between two outputs of the same model, not error. Errors both share (drift, scale, a wrong prior) would get certified, so the claimed coverage guarantee would be vacuous with respect to true error.

What survives:
1. **Prequential self-labels.** Each incoming frame was, one step earlier, an unvisited pose. Predicting it from G and R before ingesting it, then scoring against what arrives, gives free calibration labels from the true query distribution, with no covariate-shift weighting. Labels can come from sensor depth where it exists (7-Scenes, ScanNet, TUM), or from the model's own pointmap once the frame is ingested. That is a weaker label, reported separately.
2. **An online, per-pixel conformal router over three sources (generate, retrieve, abstain), inside a streaming memory.** The audit and VSCP are offline, use a single source, and need held-out GT.
3. **Regenerability as the eviction criterion for the keyframe store**, against Stream3D-style evidence and coverage eviction at equal budget.
4. **A measured crossover of generation against retrieval, tied to the gate horizon.** No search result routes between generated and retrieved spatial memory using a calibrated bound.

The defensible delta is items 1 to 3, framed as memory management (which store answers, what the store may forget), not as uncertainty estimation. This matters because the audit, Trust3R and GeoCond crowd the uncertainty-estimation space. It also connects directly to #8, the conformal do-no-harm gate, which this carries from text memory to spatial memory, and to #3, the delayed self-test eviction.
newIdeas.revised_mechanism:
Setup: a frozen CUT3R (cut3r_512_dpt_4_64) with the TTT3R update rule. Four sources answer each spatial query:
- **G:** a raymap query of the live state, with the update turned off.
- **R:** z-buffered reprojection of the stored keyframe pointmaps, with at most B keyframes.
- **RG (optional):** a copy of the state with the retrieved keyframes injected, then queried.
- **L:** abstain.

**Prequential loop** (the core change from the original):
- At each step t, before ingesting frame t+1, query G and R at frame t+1's pose. Place the pose in the model's frame with a Sim(3) fitted to the trajectory up to t, as in #13's protocol, and also report an oracle that uses the model's own later pose estimate, so alignment error can be separated out.
- After ingesting the frame, compute per-pixel errors for G and R against:
  - (a) sensor depth where available, which is the primary label;
  - (b) the model's own pointmap of the new frame, which is the GT-free label, reported with its known bias.
- Also add delayed labels: queries at past poses (lags of 10 to 1000) scored against sensor depth.

**Error score:** a small logistic or isotonic model, fitted online, over:
- raymap confidence;
- frustum overlap with the store;
- lag since the surface was last observed;
- the TTT3R gate statistics;
- G-R disagreement.

**Calibration:** online split-conformal or adaptive conformal inference (ACI) quantiles of the score's residuals. Coverage is checked per view as well as per pixel, following VSCP's lesson.

**Router:** use G where the bound is at most epsilon. Otherwise use R if the store covers the pixel with a bound at most epsilon. Otherwise abstain (L).

**Residual store:**
- Admit a keyframe when G's prequential error on it exceeds epsilon.
- Evict a stored keyframe when G regenerates its view within epsilon at a delayed re-test (the 3D twin of #3).

**Baselines at equal B:**
- FIFO eviction;
- facility-location coverage eviction;
- Stream3D-style evidence scoring;
- a router that uses raw confidence with one global post-hoc temperature, which is the audit-style fix.
newIdeas.revised_first_experiment:
About 8 GPU-hours over 2 weeks, inference only.
- Days 1 to 3: in a TTT3R fork, check that ray_mask and update-off raymap queries leave the state unchanged. Add z-buffer reprojection of keyframes.
- Days 4 to 9, prequential run:
  - Data: all of 7-Scenes and 5 ScanNet v2 loop scenes, using sensor depth.
  - Schedule: at every 5th step, query G, R(B=all, 32, 8) and #13's prior control at the next frame's pose. The prior control is a raymap query from a state that never saw the region.
  - Also query at past poses, at lags of 10, 30, 100, 300 and 1000.
  - Bin the results by frustum overlap with what has been seen so far: low, mid, high.
  - Report AbsRel, delta<1.25, completeness and PSNR. Report Sim(3)-aligned and own-pose-oracle numbers separately.
- Days 10 to 14:
  - Fit the error score online and measure its AUROC for picking which of G and R wins.
  - Run ACI at a nominal 90% and report pixel-level and view-level coverage at unvisited poses.
  - Compare against the raw-confidence router and against a single global temperature fitted on the first 10% of the stream.
- GO if all three hold:
  - in the short-lag bin or the low-overlap unvisited bin, G beats the prior control by at least 15% relative AbsRel and beats R at B=8 by at least 10% (completeness-weighted);
  - the score picks the winner of G vs R with AUROC of at least 0.70;
  - prequential ACI reaches view-level coverage within 5 points of nominal at unvisited poses, where the global-temperature baseline misses by at least 10 points.
newIdeas.revised_kill_criterion:
- **Kill if G is not real memory.** G within 10% of the prior control in every bin means the generated recall is a learned prior.
- **Kill if there is nothing to route on.** Score AUROC below 0.60 for picking which of G and R wins.
- **Kill the calibration claim if it adds nothing over the audit's fix.** Prequential ACI must beat a single global post-hoc temperature, fitted once, by at least 5 points of view-level coverage at unvisited poses. If it does not, the result reduces to the audit (2608.29705) plus a router, which is too thin to publish.
- **If only the regenerability-eviction part fails:** that means it does not beat both coverage and evidence eviction by at least 10% AbsRel at equal B. Drop the eviction claim and write the routing result up as a section of #13.

original.title: Generate, retrieve, or look: calibrated generative recall from a streaming 3D state
original.one_liner: Treat the CUT3R/TTT3R raymap read-out as memory generation and an explicit keyframe store as memory retrieval. For each spatial query, at a past pose or an unvisited one, choose between generating, retrieving and 'go look'. The choice uses a conformal error bound that the agent calibrates online from its own past views. Then keep in the store only what generation gets wrong.
original.survey_cell: Working/Factual x Latent: the survey's 'latent memory generation' sub-area (MemGen, VisMem) set against a token-level store. Position 7.1 (from memory retrieval to memory generation); frontiers: memory for world models, trustworthy memory.
original.survey_hook: Survey 7.1 argues that agents should synthesize memory on demand rather than look it up, and it lists memory for world models and trustworthy memory (hallucination) as frontiers. The world-model-style memories in its list all work on the retrieval side: Context as Memory retrieves past frames by FOV overlap for scene-consistent video generation, and MemoryVLA retrieves from a memory bank. A streaming 3D model that can be queried at any camera is a generative spatial memory: CUT3R predicts colored pointmaps at virtual views from its state. Nothing in the survey's list asks when such a generated memory should be trusted over a retrieved one, or what it lets the store forget.
original.big_picture_hook:
- Generation reads from the fast state (the doc's 'fixed capacity, lost when the session ends' row). Retrieval reads from the external store (the 'retrieval interference and drift' row). The router decides per query which store answers, which turns the doc's four-store map into a policy.
- The doc's 3D section reads TTT3R's state as fast weights. ZipMap (2603.04385) stores a scene in TTT fast weights that can be queried at novel cameras, so generative read-out is becoming standard.
- 'Storage was never the constraint' reframes the eviction part: the point is not saving bytes, but that retrieval cannot answer unvisited poses at any store size.
- The calibrated bound carries #8's do-no-harm idea from text memory to spatial memory.
original.task:
Spatial recall for an embodied agent streaming RGB through a frozen CUT3R (cut3r_512_dpt_4_64.pth) with the TTT3R update rule.
- At t in {200, 500, 1000}, predict depth and color at three kinds of query camera:
  - (i) past poses, at lags of 10 to 1000 frames;
  - (ii) unvisited nearby poses, taken from future GT frames and binned by frustum overlap with everything seen so far;
  - (iii) far or unseen poses, where the correct answer is to abstain.
- Queries are placed in the model's frame with #13's protocol (a Sim(3) fitted to the trajectory up to t).
- Data: 7-Scenes (all 7 scenes), 10 ScanNet v2 loop scenes, TUM fr3/long_office_household, NRGBD.
- Metrics: depth AbsRel, delta<1.25, completeness (fraction of valid pixels), PSNR of the predicted color, empirical coverage of the conformal bound, abstention rate, store size in keyframes, and the frontier of recall error against store size.
original.mechanism:
- Sources:
  - G (generation): a raymap query of the live state with the state update turned off; nothing is stored.
  - R (retrieval): z-buffered reprojection of stored keyframe pointmaps (the model's own earlier outputs) into the query camera, with a budget of B keyframes.
  - L: abstain.
  - Optional RG (retrieval-augmented generation): write the retrieved keyframe into a copy of the state, then query the copy.
- Error score: a per-pixel error predictor built from raymap confidence, the lag since the surface was last observed, overlap with the store, and the TTT3R alignment.
- Online self-calibration without GT: periodically re-query G at past keyframe poses. Its disagreement with the stored predictions gives labels for split-conformal quantiles. Weighting for covariate shift by frustum overlap carries the bound to unvisited poses.
- Router: answer from G where the bound is at most epsilon; otherwise from R if the store covers the pixel; otherwise abstain (L).
- Residual store: evict a keyframe once G regenerates its view within epsilon at a delayed re-test (the 3D twin of #3's delayed cued self-test). Compare against FIFO and facility-location coverage eviction at equal B.
original.hypothesis:
- H1 (crossover): G beats R at short lags and at unvisited low-overlap poses, where R leaves holes; R beats G at long lags. The crossover lag tracks TTT3R's gate-derived horizon (2605.16981).
- H2 (confabulation): CUT3R's raw raymap confidence is overconfident at unvisited poses: a nominal 90% bound covers less than 80%. With self-calibrated conformal routing, coverage stays at 90% +/- 3 at past poses, and at 85% or more at unvisited poses after overlap weighting.
- H3 (residual store): the router plus residual eviction matches the recall error of storing everything while keeping at most 1/3 of the keyframes, and beats coverage eviction by at least 10% AbsRel at equal B.
original.first_experiment:
About 8 GPU-hours over 2 weeks, inference only.
- Days 1-3: confirm CUT3R's ray_mask and update flags (the same check #13 needs). Fork TTT3R to add raymap queries and keyframe reprojection.
- Days 4-10: on 7-Scenes and 5 ScanNet scenes at t=500, issue 50 queries per bin (5 lag bins, 3 overlap bins). Compare G, R at B = all, 32 and 8, and #13's prior control (a raymap query issued before the region was observed).
- Days 11-14: fit the error score and measure its AUROC for picking which of G and R wins.
- GO if both hold:
  - in at least the short-lag bin or the unvisited low-overlap bin, G beats the prior control by at least 15% relative AbsRel and beats R at B=8 by at least 10% (completeness-weighted);
  - the error score picks the winner of G vs R with AUROC of at least 0.70.
original.kill_criterion:
- Kill if G is within 10% of the prior control in every bin. The 'generated memory' would then be a learned prior rather than memory, a risk #13 already names.
- Kill if the error score cannot pick the winner of G vs R (AUROC below 0.60), since there is then nothing to route on.
- If only H3 fails, drop the eviction claim and publish H1-H2 as a calibrated-routing paper.

newIdeas.title: Experience in the start state: a domain pool of CUT3R/TTT3R initial states, and how long that experience survives overwriting
newIdeas.one_liner: CUT3R/TTT3R start every scene from the same learned initial state tokens, so a deployed agent never reuses what earlier scenes taught it. The idea keeps that experience as a small, managed pool of domain-tuned start states on a frozen backbone, chosen at the first frames by a learned domain descriptor. The pool method itself is borrowed from L2P and ProtoDepth. The new part is measuring how long start-state experience survives the recurrent overwrite, and whether forgetting moves from the weights to picking the wrong pool entry.

closest_work.title: ProtoDepth: Unsupervised Continual Depth Completion with Prototypes (2503.12745)
closest_work.overlap: The strongest scoop on the method. A frozen pretrained depth model gets one learned prototype set per domain. When the domain is not labeled, learned domain descriptors pick the prototype set at test time. It covers indoor and outdoor domains, is unsupervised, and cuts forgetting by about 52%. That is the pool, key retrieval, frozen backbone and BWT story of arm M2, already published for depth completion (a single-frame, non-recurrent model). Our pool cannot claim novelty as a pool-management method.

closest_work.title: UnCLe: Unsupervised Continual Learning of Depth Completion (2410.18074)
closest_work.overlap: An existing indoor/outdoor domain-incremental depth benchmark with forgetting metrics. The A-B-A domain stream is not a new protocol idea outside streaming 3D.

closest_work.overlap: Online continual monocular depth across real domains with a diversity-sampled replay buffer. This covers arm M5 (one model plus clip replay) for depth.

closest_work.overlap: Initial-state tuning is already a named PEFT method for recurrent models. For S4 it is proven equivalent to prefix tuning, and it is found weaker than LoRA. This predicts H4 (the start state loses to LoRA). It also means a 'warm-up prefix of in-domain frames' baseline is required, since a tuned start state may only be a compressed prefix.

closest_work.overlap: Uses Initial State Tuning as a standard baseline for Mamba/Mamba-2. Tuning a recurrent start state is not new as a mechanism.
